records.qtitle: Irrigated land in the country
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that there has been an increase in irrigated land during the last three years; and<br/><br/>(b)	 if so, the details of the increase thereof, State-wise?	<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE <br/><br/>(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH  SHEKHAWAT)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	 Yes Sir. As per the latest data available on land use statistics, there has been an increase in net irrigated area and gross irrigated area at all India level during the last three years from 2012-13 to 2014-15. State-wise details of net irrigated area and gross irrigated area in the country for the years 2012-13 to 2014-15 is given at Annexure. 	<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Dependency on agriculture
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that most of the families of the country are still dependent on agriculture; and<br/><br/>(b)	 if so, the total number of farmers, in crore, who are engaged in agricultural activities, State-wise?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE <br/><br/>(SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH  SHEKHAWAT)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	 As per the ‘Situation Assessment Survey of Agricultural Household’, 2013 conducted by National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) in its 70th round,  agricultural households constitute 57.8 percent of the total estimated rural households of the country. records.qtitle: NRC in Assam

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):	Sir;  The complete Draft National Register for Citizens (NRC) in the State of Assam has been published on 30.07.2018. records.qtitle: Dues of corporate houses under NPAs
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the total number of corporate houses whose dues under NPAs are over Rupees one           thousand crores;<br/>(b) the details thereof;<br/>(c) the number of corporate houses against which action is being taken; and<br/>(d) the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a) to (d): Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has apprised that it does not have the required information regarding the number of corporate houses whose dues under Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) are over Rs. 1,000 crore and the number against which action is being taken. <br/>As regards NPAs over Rs. 1,000 crore, RBI has further informed that as per data submitted by Scheduled Commercial Banks, as on 31.3.2018, there were 139 borrowers with aggregate gross NPAs of more than Rs. 1,000 crore. <br/>As regards action taken against corporates, RBI has additionally apprised that it issued directions to banks on 15.6.2017, instructing them to file applications for initiation of corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC) in respect of 12 borrowers, which had cumulative fund-based and non-fund-based outstanding amount of Rs. 1,97,769 crore as on 31.3.2017. It subsequently issued further directions to banks advising them to finalise and implement resolution plans in respect of 29 accounts by 13.12.2017, failing which these too had to be referred for CIRP under IBC. The cumulative fund-based and non-fund-based outstanding amount for these accounts was Rs. 1,35,846 crore, as on 30.6.2017.<br/>In addition to action on the instructions of RBI as above, banks have themselves taken action for recovery/resolution against other corporate defaulters, under legal mechanisms such as the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, Debts Recovery Tribunals and IBC.<br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Loan before 2014 turned into NPAs
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: a)	whether it is a fact that banks are financially in weak position owing to NPA accounts;<br/>b)	the number of NPA accounts out of these NPA accounts of Banks for which loans were sanctioned before 2014 and the quantum of that loan as on date; and<br/>c)	the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a): Banks are positioned strongly in terms of their deposit base, diversified credit growth, healthy and improving net interest margin, and substantial capital base. As per RBI data, as on 20.7.2018, Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) had aggregate deposits of Rs. 114.38 lakh crore, which was 32.8% more than their aggregate credit, reflecting customer confidence and a strong fund base. This is being deployed for diversified credit growth of 12.4% year-on-year, as on 20.7.2018, which will help further improve net interest margin from the existing healthy level of 2.7% as of March 2018. Further, as per RBI data, SCBs had a capital to risk-weighted asset ratio of 13.8% as of March 2018, as against the regulatory norm of 10.875%.<br/>(b) and (c): With regard to the number of NPA accounts of banks for which loans were sanctioned before 2014 and the quantum of loans in those accounts as on date, RBI has informed that it does not collect data on NPAs based on the original date of sanction of loans and as such, it does not have information with reference to any particular date of disbursal.<br/>RBI has also apprised that it may be observed from the data that there is a sharp increase in NPAs during 2015-16, mainly due to Asset Quality Review (AQR) undertaken by RBI with the help of newly introduced large borrower database (CRILC) which provides system-wide view of a borrower and, thus, enabled better identification of NPA hitherto not recognised by banks.<br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Production of Tejas aircraft
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the total time required and cost incurred to manufacture Tejas fighter planes;<br/><br/><br/>(b) the total number of Tejas fighter planes handed over to the Indian Air Force, so far;<br/><br/>(c) the future plans with respect to these fighter planes; and<br/><br/>(d) the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  For production of  Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas, Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has got orders from Indian Air Force (IAF) for 40 aircrafts {20 Initial Operational Clearance (IOC) standard and 20 Final Operational Clearance (FOC) standard}.  20 IOC contract was signed on 31st March 2006 to be completed by December 2011 and 20 FOC contract was signed on 23rd December 2010 to be completed by 2016.  IOC for LCA Tejas was received in December, 2013.<br/><br/>The value of IOC contract for 20 No. Tejas aircrafts is Rs.2701.70 Crores (Revised to Rs.2812.91 Crores).  Amendment in IOC contract has been sought for Rs.5362.17 Crores as part of Change Order on account of changes in build standards for Integration entailing procurement of additional Line Replaceable Units (LRUs), Raw materials, composite materials, Bought out items and consumables, tooling etc.<br/><br/>The value of FOC contract for 20 Tejas aircrafts is Rs.5989.39 Crores.<br/>Out of total 20 IOC aircrafts, 9 aircrafts have been delivered by HAL to IAF till date.<br/><br/>(c) & (d):  Besides, 40 LCA Tejas aircrafts (20 IOC & 20 FOC), Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) has cleared acquisition of 83 LCA Mk1A aircraft with enhanced capabilities with Active Electronically Scanned Array (AESA) Radar, Beyond Visual Range (BVR) Missile, Self-Protection Jammer (SPJ) and Air-to-Air Refuelling (AAR) for which quotation has been submitted by HAL.<br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Sale of shares of Mother Dairy
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether there was any proposal to sell whole or part of the shares of Mother Dairy Fruits and Vegetables to private company during the UPA regime;<br/>(b)	 if so, Government''s view at that time;<br/>(c)	 whether it is a fact that the benefits of research in mustard have been passed on to the same group by NDDB; and<br/>(d)	 whether Government would enquire into a possbile conflict of interest through a Central investigation agency?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/><br/>MINISTER FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>(SHRI RADHA MOHAN SINGH)<br/><br/>  (a) to (d): A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (a) TO (d) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.195 FOR 03.08.2018 REGARDING SALE OF SHARES OF MOTHER DAIRY.<br/>	<br/>(a)	  As per information received from National Dairy Development Board(NDDB), no such  records are available with NDDB.<br/><br/>(b)	Does not arise, in view of (a) above.<br/><br/>(c)	 No Sir.  The Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants set up by the Delhi University, with financial support of  NDDB was involved in improvement of Rapeseed-Mustard from 1996 to September 2016. The outcomes of the Project have been patented and the patent rights are jointly held by NDDB and the Delhi University.<br/><br/>(d)	Does not arise, in view of (c) above.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Non privatization of Mother Dairy
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether Mother Dairy was set up under the NDDB Act to help the farmers;<br/>(b) if so, the quantum of milk purchased respectively from farmers, farmers'' cooperatives, farmers'' producer companies and private companies during the years 2004—2014, year-wise;<br/>(c) the average purchase price paid to these sources, category-wise and yearwise; and<br/>(d) the action Government proposes to take to ensure retaining Mother Dairy as a farmers'' organisation and not a private company with monopoly shareholding?<br/>
records.ans_text: A N S W E R<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE & FARMERS WELFARE<br/>(SHRIMATI KRISHNA RAJ)<br/><br/>(a)	As per the provisions of the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) Act, 1987, Mother Dairy, Delhi as a subsidiary unit of NDDB. The objective of Mother Dairy is to provide quality food and beverages to consumers at affordable prices while assuring fair returns to farmers.<br/><br/>(b)	The year-wise details of quantum of milk purchased by Mother Dairy from farmers of Cooperatives, New Generation Cooperatives, Milk Producers Companies and Private Companies during the years 2004-2014 are  Annexed.    <br/><br/>(c)	The year-wise details of purchase price of milk procured by Mother Dairy  from the farmers of Cooperatives, New Generation Cooperatives, Milk Producers Companies and Private Companies during the years 2004-2014 are  Annexed.   <br/><br/>(d)	The provisions of Section 42 of the NDDB Act, 1987, provides that Mother Dairy to be a subsidiary unit of NDDB. Further, NDDB Board decided that the Mother Dairy be made a wholly owned subsidiary company of the NDDB. The chairman of NDDB is the Non- executive chairman of Mother Dairy, and one Director of NDDB, selected from NDDB is on the Board of Directors of Mother Dairy Fruit & Vegetable Private Limited. As per Section 42 of NDDB Act, 1987, any change in the special character of Mother Dairy has to be decided by NDDB Board, where apart from others, one director from amongst officials of Central Government and two Directors from amongst Chairman of State Cooperative Dairy Federations are also present.<br/>*****

records.qtitle: Administrative Reforms Commission
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether Government has accepted the suggestions contained in the report of Administrative Reforms Commission headed by Shri Veerappa Moily; <br/>(b) 	if so, the status thereof in terms of implementation; and <br/>(c) 	the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS AND MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE<br/>(DR. JITENDRA SINGH)<br/><br/>(a) to (c): A statement is laid on the table of the House.<br/><br/><br/>*******<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 177 FOR 02.08.2018 REGARDING ADMINISTRATIVE REFORMS COMMISSION<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):  The Second Administrative Reforms Commission (2ndARC) was constituted on 31.08.2005, as a Commission of Inquiry, under the Chairmanship of Shri Veerappa Moily, for preparing a detailed blueprint for revamping the public administration system in the country.  The other Members were as under:-<br/><br/>(i)	Shri V. Ramachandran.<br/>(ii)	Dr. A.P. Mukherjee.<br/>(iii)	Dr. A.H. Kalro, Member.<br/>(iv)	Dr.Jayaprakash Narayan, Member.<br/>(v)	Smt. VineetaRai, IAS, Member Secretary.<br/><br/>2.	The 2ndARC presented 15 reports at different point of times containing recommendations on the following:-<br/><br/>(i)	Right to Information – Master Key to Good Governance.<br/>(ii)	Unlocking Human Capital: Entitlements and Governance – a Case Study.<br/>(iii)	Crisis Management.<br/>(iv)	Ethics in Governance.<br/>(v)	Public Order.<br/>(vi)	Local Governance.<br/>(vii)	Capacity Building for Conflict Resolution – Friction to Fusion.<br/>(viii)	Combating Terrorism (being handled by the Ministry of Home Affairs)<br/>(ix)	Social Capital – A Shared Destiny.<br/>(x)	Refurbishing of Personnel Administration – Scaling New Heights<br/>(xi)	Promoting e-Governance – The Smart Way Forward<br/>(xii)	Citizen Centric Administration - The Heart of Governance<br/>(xiii)	Organisational Structure of Government of India<br/>(xiv)	Strengthening Financial Management System<br/>(xv)	State and District Administration<br/><br/>3.	The procedure prescribed for processing of the recommendations made by 2ndARC was that the recommendations were first considered by the concerned administrative Ministries/Departments.The views of the concerned Ministries/Departments were then considered by the Core Group on Administrative Reforms (CGAR) headed by the Cabinet Secretary.  Subsequently, they were placed before the Group of Ministers (GOM) for its consideration and a final decision.<br/><br/>4.	The Group of Ministers considered 14reports of 2ndARC through the Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances (DAR&PG).  The Eighth Report on the subject of ‘Combating Terrorism’ was separately handled by the Ministry of Home Affairs.  In the 14Reports processed through the DARPG, there were 1491 recommendations, out of which 1183 were accepted, 228 were not accepted and 59 were deferred. 21 recommendations were referred to other foras. The decisions of GOM were then communicated to all the concerned administrative Ministries/Departments in the Government of India and to all the State/UT Governments for taking necessary action for implementation.   <br/><br/>5.	The Action Taken Reports (ATRs) furnished by various Ministries/Departments and the States/UTs on the accepted recommendations contained in all the 14 reportswas then placed before the Cabinet.  The Cabinet took note of the status of action taken in respect of all the 14 reports on the following dates:<br/><br/>(i)	1stand 3rdReports in its meeting held on 29.12.2009.<br/>(ii)	2ndReport in its meeting held on 03.12.2009<br/>(iii)	6thReport in its meeting held on 30.06.2011<br/>(iv)	4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, and 15thReports in its meeting held on 13.03.2014. <br/><br/><br/><br/>******<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Sub plan for development of tribals
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that Government has directed to formulate a sub plan for development of tribals; and <br/><br/>(b)	 if so, by when it would be formulated and what would be its format?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) & (b): 	Tribal Sub Plan (TSP), now called Scheduled Tribe Component (STC) Strategy was adopted in 5th Five Year Plan (1974-75) for accelerated development of tribal people. It envisages channelizing the flow of outlays & benefits from all sectors of development to ST population. STC is a multi-pronged strategy which includes support for education, health, sanitation, water supply, livelihood etc. Major part of infrastructure development in tribal dominated areas and provision of basic amenities to tribal people in the country is carried out through various schemes / programmes of concerned Central Ministries and the State Governments concerned, while the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides additive to these initiatives by way of plugging gaps.<br/><br/>Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) has issued revised norms on 26.12.2017 for allocation of STC by Central Ministries / Departments. As per Union Budget 2018-19, there are 37 Central Ministries and Departments having STC funds catering to specific tribal development in various sectors through 299 different schemes. <br/><br/>So far as State TSP is concerned, as per extant Guidelines, State Governments are to allocate funds under TSP out of total Plan/Scheme Outlays not less than the population proportion of STs in State as per 2011 Census. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Unearthing of black money
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that Government has initiated harsh penal proceedings against black money; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c) the quantum of black money unearthed till date on account of such steps and the total money recovered in this regard; and <br/>(d) the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR FINANCE<br/>(SHRI SHIV PRATAP SHUKLA)<br/>(a) & (b): The Income-tax Department takes appropriate action against black money which is an on-going process.  Such action under the direct tax laws includes searches, surveys, enquiries, assessment of income, levy of penalties and filing of prosecution complaints before criminal courts, wherever applicable. <br/>Moreover, recognizing the limitations of the Income-tax Act, 1961, etc. in dealing with black money stashed abroad, the Government enacted a comprehensive and a more stringent new law namely The Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015 that has come into force w.e.f. 01.07.2015. It provides for separate taxation of undisclosed foreign income and assets. Most importantly, apart from providing more stringent provisions for penalty and prosecution, for the first time, this law has included the offence of willful attempt to evade tax etc. in relation to undisclosed foreign income/assets as a Scheduled Offence under the Prevention of Money-laundering Act, 2002 (PMLA).<br/><br/>The details of prosecution proceedings initiated by the ITD under the relevant provisions of the Income Tax Act, 1961, during the last three F.Y.s are as under:-<br/>Financial Year	No. of cases in which prosecution complaints filed	Cases compounded	No. of persons convicted<br/>1	2	4	5<br/>2015-16	552	1019	28<br/>2016-17	1252	1208	16<br/>2017-18 	4527	1621	68<br/>(c) & (d):  The details of search & seizure and surveys conducted by the Income Tax Department in the last three F.Y.s are as under:<br/>Search and seizure:<br/>Financial Year	Number of groups searched	Total assets seized (In Rs. crore)	Undisclosed income admitted u/s 132(4) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 [in Rs. crore]<br/>2015-16	447	712.32	11226<br/>2016-17	1152	1469.62	15497<br/>2017-18*	581	997.17	15755<br/>*Figures are provisional<br/>Surveys:<br/>Financial Year	No. of surveys conducted	Undisclosed income detected (in Rs. crore)<br/>2015-16	4428	9700<br/>2016-17	12520	13690<br/>2017-18	13547	9638<br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Unearthing of benami properties
records.name: Harivansh

records.qtitle: Construction of Ranchi Tata four lane road
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the Ranchi-Tata four lane road is under construction for many years; <br/><br/>(b)	if so, by when would it be completed; and<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a)	The work for 4-laning of Ranchi-Rangoan-Jamshedpur stretch was awarded on BOT Annuity mode in April, 2011 and the construction started in December, 2012 with construction period of 30 months.<br/><br/>(b) & (c)	The work could not be completed within scheduled time due to delay in land acquisition, forest clearance and poor performance/slow progress of the Concessionaire on account of financial crunch. Cure period notice has been issued to the Concessionaire. Further, the progress of work is being also monitored by Hon’ble High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi. It has been decided to terminate the ongoing Concession Agreement and get the residual project work completed on EPC mode. Accordingly, an affidavit to this effect has been filed in the Hon’ble High Court of Jharkhand at Ranchi thereby requesting to permit the termination of Concession Agreement and get the residual project work completed on EPC mode. The case was heard on 25-07-2018 and next date of hearing has been given by the Hon’ble High Court as 09-08-2018.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: (clubbed) Vacant posts in Supreme Court, High Courts and subordinate judiciary
records.name: D. Kupendra Reddy
records.qn_text: (a) whether there are more than 6000 vacant posts in the subordinate judiciary in lower courts of the country;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof, State-wise, and the reasons for keeping these posts vacant since long;<br/>(c) whether a large number of posts of Judges are vacant in the High Courts and in the Supreme Court;<br/>(d) if so, the details thereof, as of now, Court-wise;<br/>(e) whether Government has taken any firm decision to fill up these vacant posts in all the courts of the country; and<br/>(f) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW AND JUSTICE AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI P. P. CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): As per information made available by the High Courts and respective State Governments, the State/UT-wise details, the sanctioned strength,the working strength and the number of vacancies of Judicial Officers of District and Subordinate Courts as on 31.03.2018 is annexed at Annexure – I.<br/>As per the Constitutional framework, the selection and appointment of judges in subordinate courts is the responsibility of the High Courts and the State Governments concerned.  In so far as recruitment of judicial officers in the States is concerned, respective High Courts do it in certain States, whereas the High Courts do it in consultation with the State Public Service Commissions in other States.<br/>The Department of Justice had written a letter in March, 2018 to the Registrars General of High Courts as well as the State Governments to share the action plan for 2018-19 to fill up vacancies in subordinate judiciary.  All the High Courts have shared the action plan which they propose to follow for filling up the  vacancies in subordinate judiciary in the year 2018-19.  The Sanctioned strength of Judicial Officers in District and Subordinate Courts has increased from 19,518 as on 31.12.2013 to 22,545 as on 31.03.2018 and the Working strength of Judicial Officers in District and Subordinate Courts has increased from 15,115 as on 31.12.2013 to 17,109 as on 31.03.2018.<br/><br/>(c) & (d) The details of sanctioned and working strength of Judges in Supreme Court and High Courts as on 23.07.2018 are annexed at Annexure-II.<br/>(e) & (f): Filling up of vacancies in the Supreme Court and the High Courts is a continuous and collaborative process, between the Executive and the Judiciary.  It requires consultation and approval from various Constitutional Authorities.  Initiation of proposal for appointment of Judges in the Supreme Court vests with the Chief Justice of India, whereas the initiation of proposals for appointment of Judges in the High Courts vests with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. While every effort is made to fill up the existing vacancies expeditiously, vacancies in High Courts keep on arising on account of retirement, resignation or elevation of Judges (to the Supreme Court) and also due to increase in the strength of Judges. records.qtitle: Pending cases in High Courts and subordinate courts
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the total number of cases pending in High Courts and the subordinate courts for last ten years or more;<br/>(b) the details thereof; and<br/>(c) the steps being taken by Government to address the same?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>MINISTER OF STATE FOR LAW AND JUSTICE AND CORPORATE AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI P. P. CHAUDHARY)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): Data on pendency of cases in the High Courts and District / Subordinate Courts is maintained by the respective High Courts.  As per information available as on 23.07.2018 on the web-portal of National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG), 9.94 lakh cases were pending in various High Courts for more than 10 years.  High Court-wise details of such cases are  at Annexure – I.  As on 23.07.2018, 22.90 lakh cases were  pending in various District and Subordinate courts of the country (excluding State / Union Territories of Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Lakshadweep and Puducherry) for more than 10 years.  State / UT – wise details of such cases  are  at Annexure -II.<br/><br/>(c): The Central Government has taken several steps to provide an ecosystem for faster disposal of cases by the judiciary.  The National Mission for Justice Delivery and Legal Reforms established by the Government has adopted a coordinated approach for phased liquidation of arrears and pendency in judicial administration through various strategic initiatives, including improving infrastructure for courts, leveraging information, communication and technology (ICT) for better justice delivery, and filling up of vacant positions of Judges in High Courts and Supreme Court.  The major achievements during the last four years are as follows.<br/>(i)  As on date, Rs. 6,302 crores have been released since the inception of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) for Development of Infrastructure Facilities for Judiciary in 1993-94. Out of this, Rs.2,858 crore (which is 45.35% of the total amount released till date) has been released to the States and UTs since April, 2014.  The number of court halls has increased from 15,818 as on 30.06.2014 to 18,444 as on date and number of residential units has increased from 10,211 as on 30.06.2014 to 15,853 as on date under this scheme.  In addition, 2,709 court halls and 1,472 residential units are under construction.  The Central Government has approved continuation of the Scheme beyond the 12th Five Year Plan period i.e. from 01.04.2017 to 31.03.2020 with an estimated additional outlay of Rs.3,320 crore.<br/>(ii) Number of computerised District & Subordinate courts has increased from 13,672 to 16,089 registering an increase of 2,417 during 2014 to 2018.  <br/>(iii) National Judicial Data Grid (NJDG) has been made accessible to   provides citizens to provide  online information about case filings, case status and electronic copies of orders and judgments from district and subordinate courts that have already been computerized. Information regarding 10.15 crore including 2.75 crore pending cases and more than 6.97 crore orders / judgments are available on this portal.  <br/>(iv) eCourts services such as details of case registration, cause list, case status, daily orders & final judgments are available to litigants and advocates through eCourts web portal, Judicial Service Centres (JSC) in all computerised courts, eCourts Mobile App with facility of QR Code (6.8 lakhs downloads), email service, SMS push & pull services. eCourts Project has been consistently amongst the top 5 Mission Mode Projects of country with a total number of transactions during Phase II at 127.06 crore.<br/>(v) During May 2014 – 23 July 2018, 18 Judges were appointed in Supreme Court; 349 new Judges were appointed and 316 Additional Judges were made Permanent in the High Courts. Sanctioned strength of Judges of High Courts has been increased from 906 in May, 2014 to 1079 currently. Similarly the sanctioned strength of Judicial Officers in District and Subordinate Courts has been  increased from 19,518 as on 31.12.2013 to 22,545 as on 31.03.2018. Further,the working strength of Judicial Officers in District and Subordinate Courts has  increased from 15,115 as on 31.12.2013 to 17,109 as on 31.03.2018.<br/>(vi) Further, in pursuance of resolution passed in Chief Justices’ Conference held in April, 2015, Arrears Committees have been set up in 24 High Courts to clear cases pending for more than five years.  Arrears Committees have been set up under District Judges too. An Arrears Committee has been constituted in the Supreme Court also to formulate steps to reduce pendency of cases in High Courts and District Courts.<br/>(vii) In order to reduce cases pending in courts for over 10 years, the Government launched the Nyaya Mitra Scheme in April 2017. Under the Scheme, retired judicial officers are engaged and designated as ‘Nyaya Mitra’ to facilitate expeditious disposal of the cases pending over 10 years.  In the first Phase, 15 Nyaya Mitras  have been engaged in 15 Districts of Rajasthan, West Bengal, Bihar, UP and Tripura.<br/>(viii) An amount of Rs.330 crore has been released to National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) during 2014 to 2018 which is the highest ever. 140.63 lakh pending cases have been settled by National Lok Adalats during 2015 to 2017. 86.14 lakh pending cases have been and 103.73 lakh pre-litigative cases were settled in Regular Lok Adalats during 2015-16 to 2017-18. 3.21 lakh pre-litigative cases were relating to public utility services were settled in Permanent Lok Adalats during 2015-16 to 2017-18.<br/>**************<br/> <br/>Annexure - records.qtitle: (clubbed) Home delivery of subsidized foodgrains
records.name: Sushil Kumar Gupta
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has any proposal to ask the State Governments to provide home delivery of highly subsidized foodgrains to the Public Distribution System (PDS) beneficiaries to avoid instances of starvation deaths in the country;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof;<br/>(c) the other reforms which the State Governments have been asked to pursue urgently in order to strengthen the PDS; and<br/>(d) whether any guidelines have been issued to the State Governments to ensure that there are no starvation deaths because of non-delivery of PDS grains?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI C. R. CHAUDHARY)<br/>(a) to (d) To ensure assured regular supply of subsidized foodgrains to beneficiaries through Public Distribution System (PDS), several reform measures have been undertaken since the inception of National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA). Government is implementing a scheme on ''End-to-End Computerization of PDS Operations'' with an aim to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of PDS and to address challenges of leakages and diversion of foodgrains, fake/bogus ration cards etc. Key components of the scheme are digitization of ration cards/beneficiaries, automation of supply chain management, online grievance redressal and automation of fair price shops (FPSs) by use of electronic point of sale (ePoS) devices.<br/>Government has been regularly issuing advisories/instructions to States/UTs to review their lists of beneficiaries under NFSA, launch special drives to issue ration cards to the weaker sections of the society and ensure supply of foodgrains through PDS to all eligible beneficiaries.<br/>Government has issued instruction to the States/UTs to put in place special dispensation for distribution of foodgrains to beneficiaries who are unable to visit the FPS for reasons such as old age, physical disability, etc. by adopting either Home Delivery of foodgrains through the FPS dealer or Delivery of foodgrains through authorized nominees of such beneficiaries.<br/>***

records.qtitle: Uniform Common Minimum Programme in schools
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government proposes to implement a Uniform Common Minimum Programme in all schools from 2019-20 onwards to have value based education; and<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI UPENDRA KUSHWAHA)<br/> <br/>(a)&(b)	During the course of the deliberations on the theme ‘Value Education’ held during the “Chintan Shivir”, organised by the Ministry of Human Resource Development on 6th and 7th November, 2017, it was recommended that a Common Minimum Programme for Value Education in Schools may be developed.  The Common Minimum Programme would focus on the four constitutional values of Justice, Equality, Liberty and Fraternity. The approach to value education would be an integrated whole school approach which requires that the system in totality responds and adopts the value concerns and reflects them in all its functioning.<br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Banks defrauded by Nirav Modi
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the names of banks which were defrauded by Nirav modi along with the details of amount which were swindled by him from these banks;    <br/><br/>(b)	the complete details thereof; and <br/><br/>(c)	the steps being taken by Government in this regard? <br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance<br/><br/><br/>(a) and (b): As per RBI inputs, based on the fraud monitoring returns furnished by banks to RBI, the frauds attributed to Nirav Modi Group by banks, as on 30.6.2018,along with the amounts thereof in crore Rupees, are as under:<br/>Punjab National Bank	6,820.08<br/>Oriental Bank of Commerce	94.13<br/>Syndicate Bank	125.00<br/>United Bank of India	18.54<br/>Andhra Bank	29.84<br/>Corporation Bank	110.00<br/>UCO Bank	60.75<br/><br/>(c): The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has informed that it had registered two cases against Shri Nirav Modi and others for defrauding Punjab National Bank (PNB).Charge-sheets have been filed in both the cases against accused persons, including Nirav Modi. Further, Red Corner Notice has been issued by Interpol against absconding accused persons, including Nirav Modi.  <br/><br/>The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has informed that it had initiated investigation on the basis of complaints filed by PNB. Prosecution complaint has been filed in the Prevention of Money Laundering Act court, and the court has taken congnizance and issued non-bailable warrant. 15 Letters Rogatory (LRs) have been forwarded to different countries. Provisional orders for attaching property amounting to Rs. 744.38 crore have been issued for attachment of 26 immovable properties. Application for declaring Nirav Modi as a fugitive economic offender under the Fugitive Economic Offender Ordinance, 2018 has been filed.<br/><br/>The Ministry of Corporate Affairs had ordered an investigation into the affairs of 114 entities directly or indirectly associated with Nirav Modi, Mehul Choksi etc, in respect of whom PNB had filed an FIR, and has assigned the same to the Serious Fraud Investigation Office.<br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Suicide by farmers
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that farmers have committed suicide in the country on a large scale; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the efforts being made by Government to curb the incidents of suicide by farmers; and <br/><br/>(c) 	the total number of farmers who have committed suicide this year or have succumbed to starvation, the State-wise details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>(SHRI RADHA MOHAN SINGH)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c):	A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/> <br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT IN RESPECT OF PARTS (a) TO (c) OF THE RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO.  42    FOR 20.7.2018 REGARDING SUICIDE BY FARMERS.<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): 	The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) under the Ministry of Home Affairs compiles and disseminates information on suicides, in its publication titled ‘Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India’ (ADSI). These Reports on suicides are available upto 2015 on its website. The Reports for the year 2016 onwards have not been published as on date.  However, NCRB has provided data relating to suicides for the year 2016 (provisional) to this Ministry.  As per the ADSI Reports for the year 2015 and data as provided by NCRB for the year 2016 (provisional), the total number of suicides by farmers and agricultural labourers in the country State-wise is at Annexure-I. The number of suicide by farmers and agricultural labourers during 2016 has come down approximately by 9.77% from 12602 to 11370. No data has been provided  by the NCRB on suicides committed by  farmers and agricultural labourers due to starvation.<br/>            Agriculture is a State subject. Agrarian distress can be addressed by enabling the farmers to increase their income.  The Government is targeting to double the income of the farmers by the year 2022.  To achieve this, the Department of Agriculture, Cooperation and Farmers’ Welfare has taken a number of measures. The Government has been reorienting the agriculture sector by focusing on an income-centeredness which goes beyond achieving merely the targeted production. The income approach focuses on achieving high productivity, reduced cost of cultivation and remunerative price on the produce, with a view to earn higher profits from farming. Various initiatives by way of schemes and policy reforms have been rolled out in consonance with this approach.  Further, these initiatives are supported by a big jump in the much needed budgetary allocations for the agriculture sector. For the period 2009-2014, the budget for agriculture was Rs.1,21,082 crore. During 2014-2019, the allocation has been enhanced by 74.5 per cent to Rs.2,11,694 crore. Besides, Non-budgetary resources have been mobilized to supplement budgetary resources.  Following are the corpus fund created during 2014-19:<br/>Contd...2/-<br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/>•	Long Term Irrigation Fund (LTIF) to complete long pending 99 irrigation projects and create 7.6 million ha of irrigation by December 2019 - Rs.40,000 crore (2016-17 and 2017-18). The total investment is expected to be Rs. 80,000 crore (approx) <br/>•	Micro Irrigation Fund for water use efficiency - Rs.5,000 crore (2017-18) <br/>•	Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund - Rs.10,881 crore (2017-18) <br/>•	Fisheries and Aqua Culture Infrastructure Development Fund - Rs.7,522.48 crore (2018-19)<br/>•	Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund – Rs.2,450 crore (2018-19) <br/>•	Agri-Market Infrastructure Fund - Rs. 2,000 crore (2018-19).<br/><br/>    The Department has been implementing various schemes for betterment of agriculture sector such as :<br/>(i)	Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme by which the farmers can know the major and minor nutrients available in their soils which will ensure judicious use of fertilizer application and thus save input cost  of farmers. <br/><br/>(ii)	Neem Coated Urea (NCU) is being promoted to regulate use of urea, enhance availability of nitrogen to the crop and reduce cost of fertilizer application.  NCU slows down the release of fertilizer and makes it available to the crop in an effective manner. <br/>(iii)    Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is being implemented with a view to promote organic farming in the country.	<br/><br/>(iv)    Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)  was launched on 1st July, 2015 with the motto of ‘Har Khet Ko Paani’ for providing end-to-end solutions in irrigation supply chain, comprising water sources, distribution network and farm level applications. <br/><br/>(v)	Electronic National Agriculture  Market (e-NAM ) which is an innovative market process to revolutionize agri-markets by ensuring better price discovery, bringing in transparency and competition     to enable farmers to get improved    remuneration for their produce moving towards<br/>Contd…3/-<br/><br/>-3-<br/> ‘One Nation One Market’. The Department has achieved the target of integration of 585 mandis with e-NAM by March 2018. Additional 200 mandies to be integrated by 2018-19 under e-NAM.   <br/><br/>(vi)	Existing 22,000 rural haats to be developed and upgraded into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs). These GrAMs, electronically linked to e-NAM portal and exempted from regulations of Agriculture Produce Marketing Committees (APMCs), will provide farmers facility to make direct sale to consumers and bulk purchasers. <br/><br/>(vii)	The Model Agricultural Produce & Livestock Marketing (Promotion & Facilitation) Act, 2017 released in April, 2017 and the Model Agricultural Produce & Livestock Contract Farming and Services (Promotion & Facilitation) Act, 2018 released in May, 2018, for adoption by State/UTs, to promote alternative competitive marketing channels for better pricing for farmers and to encourage private investment in developing efficient marketing infrastructure and value chain. <br/>(viii)	Government has introduced Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) from Kharif 2016 to address the risks associated with agriculture.  PMFBY addresses all the shortcomings in the earlier schemes and is available to the farmers at very low rates of premium. The farmers will get full insurance cover as there is no capping of sum insured and consequently the claim amount is not curtailed or reduced. This scheme provides insurance cover at all stages of the crop cycle including post-harvest risks in specified instances. <br/>(ix)  The Government provides total interest subvention up to 5% (inclusive of 3% prompt repayment incentive) on short-term crop loans up to Rs. 3.00 lakh. Thus, loan is available to farmers at a reduced rate of 4% per annum on prompt repayment.  <br/>(x)  The Government is implementing several Centrally Sponsored Schemes viz. National Food Security Mission (NFSM); Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH); National Mission on Oilseeds & Oilpalm (NMOOP); National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA); National Mission on Agricultural Extension & Technology (NMAET) and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) for benefit of farmers. <br/>Contd...4/-<br/>-4-<br/> 	Further, Minimum Support Price (MSP) is notified for both Kharif and Rabi crops based on the recommendations of the Commission on Agriculture Costs & Prices (CACP). The Commission collects & analyses data on cost of activation and recommends MSP.  In the budget <br/>for 2018-19 the Government had announced that MSP for all unannounced Kharif crops will be 1.5 times   the cost of production.  Giving a major boost for the farmers income, the  Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs  (CCEA) in its meeting held on 04.07.2018   has approved the increase in the MSPs for all Kharif crops for 2018-19 season at a level of at least 150 percent of the cost of production. The MSP declared during 2012-13 to 2018-19 for various crops is at Annexure-II.<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Late running of trains
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that important trains run late by many hours on many routes even on normal days; <br/><br/>(b) if so, the reasons therefor; <br/><br/>(c) the details of efforts being made by Government in this direction; and <br/><br/>(d) by when Railways would start running on time?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/> (SHRI RAJEN GOHAIN)<br/><br/>(a) and (b)  Since last few months, a large number of safety related track maintenance works are being undertaken for which large number of speed restrictions have been imposed. This has led to drop in punctuality of trains over Indian Railways.  For maintenance of assets and infrastructure augmentation, 4,60,566 block hours have been given during April to June 2018 as against 4,11,627 block hours during April to June 2017, which is 48,939 (11.89%) more block hours as compared to the corresponding period of 2017-18. <br/>         At times, trains get delayed not only due to the factors related to its internal working but also external factors which are beyond the control of Railways.  In addition to asset failures, certain factors such as line capacity and terminal capacity constraints on account of increasing passenger and freight traffic, adverse weather conditions (fog, rains, breaches), intermittent natural calamities such as floods, cyclones, heavy rains, heavy road traffic at level crossing gates across the Indian Railways network, mid-section run over cases involving cattle and humans etc. also adversely affect the punctuality of trains over Indian Railways.  <br/><br/>-2-<br/>(c) & (d) Focussed attention, daily, is given by the Indian Railways at the station, Division, Zonal headquarter and Railway Board levels for ensuring the punctuality of all passenger carrying trains.  <br/>         Indian Railways have taken various initiatives such as prioritization of preventive maintenance of assets to minimize asset failures, capacity enhancement projects by construction of additional loop lines at stations, doubling, construction of third line corridors, automatic signaling, construction of limited height subway to replace level crossings, Rail Under Bridges and Rail Over Bridges etc. In addition, Zonal Railways have also been advised to have better coordination with Civil and Police authorities of States to deal with situations arising out of law and order problems. In order to avoid passenger inconvenience due to late running of trains, sending of intimation through SMS regarding late running of trains has also been introduced in some trains on a trial basis. Further, provision of scratch rakes wherever operationally feasible, is also undertaken to ensure that minimum inconvenience is caused to passengers.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Construction of World Class Institutes
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state the names and details of progress made with regard to the construction of ten world class universities announced by the Central Government in the last budget?
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/>A statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/> <br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. †*22 FOR 19.07.2018 ASKED BY HON’BLE MEMBER OF PARLIAMENT SHRI HARIVANSH REGARDING CONSTRUCTION OF WORLD CLASS INSTITUTES<br/><br/>	As per the budget announcement 2016 University Grants Commission (UGC) issued / notified the UGC (Declaration of Government Educational Institutions as Institutions of Eminence) Guidelines, 2017 for public Institutions and UGC (Institution of Eminence Deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2017 for private Institutions to enable 10 public and 10 private Institutions to emerge as World Class Teaching and Research Institutions called on ‘Institutions of Eminence’ (IoEs).<br/><br/>	In accordance with the regulations, the Empowered Expert Committee (EEC) has been constituted vide order dated 20th February, 2018.  A notification seeking applications from the eligible institutions has been issued on 13th September, 2017.  Accordingly, 114 applications – 74 from public sector and 40 from private sector, including 11 applications in the Greenfield projects have been received.<br/><br/>	EEC after thorough examination of applications and presentations made by the institutions has made recommendations.<br/><br/>	The EEC report was examined by UGC in its meeting held on 9th July, 2018 and it was resolved that 3 institutions from the public category and 3 from private category may be notified in the first instance.  Accordingly, the following public institutions have been approved for notification as Institutions of Eminence (IoEs).<br/><br/>(i)	Indian Institute of Science, Bangalore<br/>(ii)	Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi<br/>(iii)	Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay<br/><br/>Further, two private institutions were recommended.<br/><br/>(i)	Birla Institute of Technology & Sciences, Pilani<br/>(ii)	Manipal Academy of Higher Education, Manipal<br/><br/>Apart from this, one institution (Jio Institute) was proposed under the Greenfield category for issue of ‘Letter of Intent’ for setting up of an institution in the next 3 years.<br/><br/>****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Promoting smart irrigation system
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that many States in the country are still extremely vulnerable to climate change due to poor irrigation system;<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the names of these States;<br/><br/>(c) 	the measures taken in the last three years to promote smart irrigation system, such as drip, sprinklers and also for spreading awareness among farmers about efficient water management; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the technical or any other assistance that has been provided to these States in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>( SHRI PARSHOTTAM RUPALA)  <br/><br/>(a) & (b):	Yes, Sir. Seasonal climate variability is a key factor affecting agriculture, particularly in the more vulnerable rainfed areas. It is estimated that out of the net sown area of the country, about 68 Million ha (48%) is irrigated and 72 Million ha (52%) is rainfed. Climate change impacts on agriculture are being witnessed all over the world, but countries like India are  more vulnerable in view of the high population depending on agriculture, pressure on natural resources and poor coping mechanisms. Yield decline are likely to be caused by shortening of growing period, negative impacts on reproduction, grain filling, decrease in water availability and poor vernalization. However adopting the improved varieties developed and input management for instance in rice, can improve yields by 6 – 17% in irrigated and 20-35% in rainfed conditions. Increase in yield have also been predicted in case of some other crops.<br/>		States namely Karnataka, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, Jharkhand, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu and Kerala having sizeable area under rainfed conditions witness drought or drought like situations.<br/>(c) & (d):	The Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana has been operationalized from 2015-16 with the motto of ‘Har Khet Ko Paani’ for providing end-to end solutions in irrigation supply chain, viz. water sources, distribution network and farm level applications. Per Drop More Crop component of PMKSY focuses on efficient use of water through adoption of precision/ micro irrigation (MI). Under this component, assistance is available to farmers for installation of micro irrigation systems viz. Drip & Sprinkler irrigation systems.       <br/><br/><br/>Contd….2/-<br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/><br/>Besides providing assistance to farmers for installation of MI systems, emphasis is given for encouraging farmers to take advantage of the scheme through press & print media, publication of leaflets/booklets, organization of workshops, exhibitions, farmer’s fairs, demonstrations through Krishi Vigayan Kendras (KVK), information on State/Government of India  portal etc. National Committee on Plasticulture Applications in Horticulture (NCPAH) with its network of 22 Precision Farming Development Centres (PFDCs) also demonstrate the benefit of precision farming including micro irrigation across the country.<br/><br/>Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has developed cost effective, location specific scientific technologies viz. rainwater harvesting and recycling, conjunctive use of rain, surface and groundwater resources, smart and precision technologies for irrigation and farming practices, optimum irrigation scheduling, resource conservation technologies and  efficient rain water harvesting structures so that the harvested water can be used for supplemental/life saving irrigation in dryland/rainfed situations.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Remunerative price for farmers produces
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that small farmers suffer from their reliance on middlemen to sell their produces; and<br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the steps which have been devised during the last three years to ensure that farmers are not compelled to sell their produces at a rate less than their cost of production?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE<br/><br/>( SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)  <br/><br/>(a) & (b):	To protect the farmers, reduce their reliance on middlemen and to ensure that farmers are not compelled to sell their produces at a rate less than their cost of production, the Government has taken a number of steps during last three years.  <br/><br/>The Government has circulated a new model “The Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion & Facilitation) Act, 2017” on 24th April, 2017 for its adoption by States/UTs. The new Model Act provides for alternative marketing channels such as direct marketing, setting up of private markets, farmer-consumer markets, special commodity markets, declaring warehouses /silos/ cold storages as market sub yards to promote agriculture marketing including ensuring against distress sale by farmers.<br/><br/>The Government has launched National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) scheme on 14th April, 2016 for transparent price discovery for the farmers for their produce through competitive online bidding system. 585 markets from 16 States and 2 UTs have been integrated with e-NAM portal by 31st March, 2018.<br/><br/>Further, as per procurement policy of the Government, the commodities such as paddy, wheat, pulses etc. offered by farmers, within the stipulated period & confirming to the specifications prescribed by Government of India, are purchased at Minimum Support Price (MSP) by the Central Government and State Government agencies. The objective of procurement by the Government agencies is to ensure that farmers get remunerative prices for their produce and do not have to resort to distress sale. <br/><br/>       In addition to above, as per Union Budget Announcement, 2018-19, it has been decided to develop and upgrade existing 22,000 rural haats into Gramin Agricultural Markets (GrAMs). These GrAMs will serve as assembly points, whereas the produce of the farmers can aggregated. Further, GrAMs will serve as platform for direct sale-purchase of agri-produce. Also, aggregated produce will be enabled to sell using online platform like that of e-NAM and shall be exempted from regulations of Agriculture Produce Marketing Committees (APMCs) for providing farmers facility to make direct sale to consumers and bulk purchasers.<br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: BBBP in Bihar and Jharkhand
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: whether it is a fact that a lot of emphasis is being laid on the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) scheme; <br/><br/>(b) 		the number of districts of the country where this scheme is currently operational; and <br/><br/>(c) 		the names of such districts in Bihar and Jharkhand?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI MANEKA SANJAY GANDHI)<br/><br/>(a) 	& (b): Yes, Sir. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao Schene (BBBP) was launched by Hon''ble Prime Minister on 22nd January, 2015,  addresses the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of women empowerment and aims to change mindsets to value girl child. It is a tri-ministerial effort of Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health & Family Welfare and Human Resource Development. The key elements of the scheme include nation-wide awareness and advocacy campaign and multi- sectoral interventions.  Multi-sectoral interventions includes strict enforcement of Pre-Conception & Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PC&PNDT) Act, Pre-Natal/ Post Natal care of mother, improve enrolment of girls in schools, construction of girls toilets, community engagement/ training etc.  BBBP Scheme is currently being implemented in 640 districts covering all the 640 districts (as per census 2011) in the Country, through Multi -sectoral intervention and alert Media &Advocacy in 405 districts and alert Media & Advocacy in 235 districts. The scheme is being administered through District appropriate authority and funds are directly being transferred to concerned Districts.<br/><br/><br/>(c):   Districts in Bihar & Jharkhand where BBBP Scheme is currently being implemented through District Administration/Authority are under:<br/><br/>State	Multi-Sectoral Intervention and Alert  Media &Advocacy outreach	Alert  Media & Advocacy outreach<br/>Bihar	*Vaishali, Patna, Muzaffarpur, Bhojpur,  Begusarai, Lakhisarai, Samastipur, Saran, Khagaria, Rohtas, Nalanda, Purba Champaran, Madhubani, Bhagalpur, Sheikhpura, Banka, Nawada (17 Districts)	Jehanabad, Munger, Sheohar, Madhepura, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga<br/>Saharsa, Buxar, Siwan, Arwal, Kaimur (Bhabua), Aurangabad, Supaul, Pashchim Champaran, Purnia, Gopalganj, Jamui, Araria, Gaya, Katihar, Kishanganj (21 Districts)<br/>Jharkhand	*Dhanbad, Hazaribagh, Giridih, Bokaro, Kodarma, Ramgarh, Ranchi<br/>Purbi Singhbhum, Palamu, Saraikela-Kharsawan, Deoghar, <br/>Jamtara (12 Districts)	Godda, Sahibganj, Garhwa, Gumla, Khunti, Dumka, Chatra<br/>Latehar, Simdega, Lohardaga, Pakur, Pashchimi Singhbhum (12 Districts)<br/><br/>* The BBBP Scheme is being implemented in District of Vaishali from State of Bihar and District of Dhanbad from State of Jharkhand since inception in January, 2015 and rest of districts have been included under BBBP Scheme after announcement of all India coverage by Hon''ble Prime Minister on 08.03.2018.<br/><br/>********<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Promotion of scientific temper and curiosity among students
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the Ministry has taken anyinitiatives to ensure that whatever is taughtin ourschools, 	colleges and universitiespromotes scientific temper and curiosityamong students;<br/>(b) 	if so, the details of such initiativestaken during the last three years; and<br/>(c) 	whether the Ministry has any planto educate students against old superstitionsand social evils	particularly in the ruralareas of the country?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI UPENDRA KUSHWAHA)<br/> <br/>(a) & (b) 	The Ministry of Human Resource Development has launched the Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan (RAA), a convergent framework across School Education and Higher Education to encourage children towards learning Science and Mathematics through activities related to Science and Mathematics. Some of the interventions under RAA for promotion of science are strengthening of school Science and Mathematics laboratories, Science Fair/Exhibition and Talent Search at district level; provision of mathematics and science kits to schools, visit of students to higher educational institutions and learning enhancement of students. <br/> <br/>        	During last three years, an amount of Rs 952.47 crore has been approved for In- service Teacher training of Maths and Science teachers at upper primary level, learning enhancement programme, computer aided learning and innovations under Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA). Further, an amount of Rs. 425.39 crore has been approved for in-service training of science and maths teachers, remedial teaching, provision of science and maths kits, science exhibitions etc under Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA). <br/> <br/>      	NITI Aayog under the Atal Innovation Mission is establishing Atal Tinkering Laboratories (ATLs) in schools across India. The objective of this scheme is to foster curiosity, creativity and imagination in young minds; and inculcate skills such as design mindset, computational thinking, adaptive learning, physical computing etc. Till date, 2441 schools have been selected across the country to establish ATLs. <br/> <br/> (c) 	The National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005, suggested a paradigm shift in science education in India. As per NCF 2005, inquiry skills should be supported and strengthened by language, design and quantitative skills. Schools should place much greater emphasis on activities aimed at stimulating investigative ability, inventiveness, creativity and transfer of learning in varied situations. The perspective of NCF-2005, on science has been translated into syllabi, textbooks and teacher support material developed by the National Council Of Educational Research And Training (NCERT). The NCERT has continuously been building capacity of science teachers and teacher educators at the secondary stage for content and pedagogies which promote inquiry, thinking and problem-solving skills in students. NCERT also conducts National Science Exhibition every year to further promote scientific temper among students.<br/><br/><br/>*****

records.qtitle: Suspension of passports of PNB scam accused
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)   	whether it is a fact that the Ministry has suspended the passports of persons accused in Punjab National Bank (PNB) scam ;<br/><br/>(b)   	whether any time has been given to them to respond;<br/><br/>(c)   	if so, whether any response has been received from them, so far;<br/><br/>(d)   	if not, what is the future course of action proposed to be taken against them; and<br/><br/>(e) 	whether the Ministry has any clue about the whereabouts of these accused?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a) 	Yes. The Ministry suspended the passports of Shri Nirav Deepak Modi and Shri Mehul Chinubhai Choksi in accordance with Section 10A of the Passports Act, 1967, on 16 February, 2018. <br/><br/>(b) to (d) 	Show Cause Notices were served on Shri Nirav Deepak Modi and Shri Mehul Chinubhai Choksi by the Passport Issuing Authority (PIA) under the Ministry on 16 February, 2018 giving them a time period of one week to respond. Since they failed to respond within the stipulated time period, their passports were revoked by the PIA under the Ministry on 23 February, 2018.<br/><br/>(e) 	The Ministry has sought the provisional arrest of Shri Nirav Deepak Modi by the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, People’s Republic of China, for which a request has been submitted to them on 23 March, 2018.<br/>

records.qtitle: Assistance to foreign tourists visiting India
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has any data about the foreign tourists visiting India in year 2017-18 and the revenue earned thereon; <br/>(b) 	what is the projection of foreign tourists visiting the country in the next three years; <br/>(c) 	what new measures have been taken to ensure that foreign tourists are not overcharged by private tour operators and others; <br/>(d) 	what directives have been sent to States for providing immediate assistance in case they need any emergency help; and <br/>(e) 	whether any cases have come to the notice of Government where certain police officials misbehaved with foreign tourists in the last one year?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TOURISM (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(SHRI K. J. ALPHONS)<br/><br/>(a):	The number of Foreign Tourist Arrivals (FTAs) in India and Foreign Exchange Earnings (FEEs) through tourism during 2017-2018 (April 2017- February 2018) is 9.45 million (provisional) and Rs.1,68,598 crore (provisional), respectively. This data is not available for March 2018.<br/><br/>(b):	No projections of Foreign Tourist Arrivals have been made for next three years.<br/><br/>(c):	Offering of tour packages is primarily a private sector activity. The Ministry of Tourism, Government of India only approves the tour operators under its voluntary scheme of Approval of Travel Trade Service Provider. Pricing of tour packages is a function of factors like supply, availability, taxation etc. and essentially works on market dynamics. As such it is not regulated by the Government. However, for any complaint, Ministry of tourism has provided a toll free helpline number 1363 available in 12 languages, to resolve any grievance of tourists including foreign tourists.<br/><br/>(d):	Ministry has issued advisories from time to time to various State Governments and UT Administrations to ensure safety and security of the tourist. <br/><br/>Further, Ministry has taken several steps for ensuring safety and security of tourists including assistance in case of any emergency, which inter-alia include the following:<br/><br/>?	Launch of 24x7 Toll Free Multi-Lingual Tourist Info-Helpline in 12 Languages to provide support service in terms of information and guidance to tourists.<br/>?	Launch of Code of Conduct for adoption by the Indian Travel and Tourism Industry for Safe and Honourable Tourism with the objective to encourage undertaking of tourism activities with respect to basic rights like dignity, safety and freedom from exploitation of both tourists and local residents, in particular women and children.<br/>?	Ministry has issued the Guidelines on Safety and Security of Tourists for States/UTs and Tips for Travelers in September 2014 to stress the importance of Safety and risk management, assist in identifying best practices and design measures to better protect tourists.<br/>?	A ‘Welcome Card’ with ‘Tips to enjoy your stay’ is being handed over to foreign tourists on arrival to make visits of tourists a memorable experience.<br/><br/>(e):	No, Sir.		 	   		<br/>                                                                 			            <br/>***********<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Plan to integrate skills and education of youths
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has any plan to integrate skills and education so that the youths of the country are well equipped to handle the present challenging employment scenario; <br/><br/>(b)	 if so, what initiatives have been taken in this regard during the last three years; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether any plan has been drawn or proposed to be drawn in collaboration with the Ministry of Human Resource Development in this regard; and <br/><br/>(d) 	if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) to (d) 	The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) in collaboration with Ministry of Human Resource has taken a number of initiatives towards integrating skills and education. Under the scheme of Vocationalisation of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education, vocational education is provided to a large number of students in selected schools. UGC is offering B.Voc. Programmes in a number of colleges/universities.  Academic Equivalence with 10th and 12th classes has been provided to ITI Students through National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) by means of credit transfer.  In addition, Degree Apprenticeships has been identified as an alternative education route by dovetailing apprenticeship component within formal education.

records.qtitle: Naxalites organising afresh in the country
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the information available with Government regarding the recent report that the naxalites are again organising afresh in different States including Kerala; <br/><br/>(b) the States in the country where naxal effect has decreased or increased; and <br/><br/>(c) the factual position of naxal effect in Bastar area?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/><br/>(a):	Change in areas of operation are resorted to from time to time by the Left Wing Extremists as part of their tactics. Their recent attempts at expansion to other parts of the country have not seen much success.<br/><br/>(b):	All States have recorded a declining trend of violence since 2010. Violence data is at Annexure attached.<br/><br/>(c):	Bastar Region remains the most important stronghold of the CPI(Maoist) accounting for approximately 36% of incidents of LWE violence and 45% of deaths in 2017. Security Forces are progressing steadily to fill the security void and regain complete control of the area. <br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>                         **********

records.qtitle: Guidelines on institutional deliveries
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has issued guidelines for the safety of the mother and child that all deliveries should be conducted by qualified persons in hospitals;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the States which have achieved this goal of 100 per cent deliveries in hospitals;<br/><br/>(c) the States which have not been able to achieve this goal; and<br/><br/>(d) what steps have been taken by Government to extend financial or other assistance to these States to achieve this goal?<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a):		Ministry has issued following guidelines to ensure safe delivery by qualified person in hospitals. <br/>•	Antenatal Care and Skilled Attendance at Birth by ANMs/LHVs/SNs. <br/><br/>•	Training of Medical Officers in Pregnancy Care and Management of Common Obstetric Complications-<br/><br/>•	Dakshata training<br/><br/>•	LaQshya – Labour room Quality improvement initiative<br/><br/>(b) & (c):	As per NFHS 4, States/UTs of Kerala, Lakshadweep and Pudduchery have achieved institutional delivery rate of 99.99%.  Detailed State and UT wise data on institutional deliveries are placed at Annexure.<br/><br/> <br/>(d):		Ministry has taken following steps to extend financial or other assistance to states to achieve this goal.<br/>•	JSY-   Janani Suraksha Yojana. Financial incentive in the form of conditional cash transfer is being given to all   BPL/SC/ST pregnant women delivering in Government health facilities/accredited private institutions  to promote institutional delivery. <br/><br/>•	JSSK- Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakaram. The initiative entitles all pregnant women delivering in public health institutions to absolutely free and no expense delivery, including caesarean section. The entitlements include free drugs and consumables, free diet, free diagnostics, free blood and free transport.  Similar entitlements were put in place for all sick infants accessing public health institutions for treatment up to 1 year of age. <br/><br/>•	MCH wings- Ministry provide financial support to state to establish 100 / 50/ 30 bedded State of the  Art MCH Wings at facilities with high delivery load to strengthen MCH services. <br/><br/>•	LaQshya- Ministry has launched LaQshya - Labour room Quality improvement Initiative. LaQshya program is a focused and targeted approach to strengthen key processes related to the labour rooms and maternity operation theatres. It will create demand generation among community to opt for institutional delivery. <br/><br/>•	Capacity Building of Staff: Ministry provide financial support to state as per their proposal to conduct various trainings like Dakshta, BeMOC, CEmOC to improve quality of services provided during delivery. <br/><br/>•	Standardization of Labour room: Ministry provide financial support to state as per their proposal to strengthen labour rooms to improve MCH services at facilities.  <br/> <br/>
