records.qtitle: Meeting of bankers in view of PNB scam
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)    whether the Ministry proposes to hold a meeting with bankers in view of the PNB financial irregularities;  <br/><br/>(b)    if so, the details thereof; <br/><br/>(c)    whether Government has sought RBI’s views on lapses in banking System; and <br/><br/>(d)    if so, the details thereof? <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>The Minister of State in the Ministry of Finance<br/><br/>(a) and (b): Government has advised public sector banks to meet and collectively prepare a report for effective management of operational risks, including technology risk, so as to safeguard against occurrence of frauds.<br/><br/>(c) and (d): With regard to the views of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on lapses in banking system, RBI has apprised that there are no ‘systemic irregularities’ in the banking sector in India, though banks may currently be faced with some transient operational issues in their functioning. RBI has further stated that, as the banking sector regulator and supervisor, it has issued detailed instructions/guidelines to banks for institutionalising robust and effective internal controls within banks, which would help minimise the incidence of frauds. <br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Participation of women in MGNREGA
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has any plan to increase the participation of women in MGNREGA schemes; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the details of steps taken in the last one year to enhance employment for women under MGNREGA schemes; and <br/><br/>(c) 	whether the Ministry has compiled any data about the number of men and women employed under this programme?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a)to (c):	The women participation rate in Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) has been 55% in FY 2015-16, 56% in FY 2016-17 and 54% in FY 2017-18 (as on 27.03.2018) which has been above the statutory requirement of 1/3rd women participation under MGNREGS.<br/><br/>The Ministry along with the States/UTs has been making all efforts for improving the women participation under the MGNREGS. During Gram Sabha and Rozgar Diwas meetings women participation is being encouraged under MGNREGS. As per Management Information System (MIS) in the current financial year 2017-18 (as on 27.03.2018), 7.45 crore individuals provided wage employment, out of which, 3.81 crore women provided employment under MGNREGS. <br/><br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Wage calculation methodology under MGNREGA
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the Ministry has any plan to persuade the Ministry of Finance to change the wage calculation methodology for schemes under MGNREGA by using Consumer Price Index-Rural instead of Rural Price Index-Agriculture Labour; <br/><br/>(b) 	whether it is a fact that earlier a high-level committee was also constituted to study this issue; and <br/><br/>(c) 	if so, the main recommendations of this Committee particularly with reference to change in wage calculation methodology for employment under MGNREGA scheme?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/><br/>(a):	The Ministry of Rural Development has proposed to change the method of indexing Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) wages to Consumer Price Index-Rural instead of the existing Consumer Price Index-Agricultural Labour (CPI-AL).<br/><br/>(b)&(c):	A Committee under the chairpersonship of Additional Secretary, Ministry of Rural Development was constituted to study among other things the appropriate index for revising MGNREGA wages. The Committee recommended using Consumer Price Index-Rural instead of the existing CPI-AL for revising MGNREGA Wages every year. The Committee also recommended use of annual average instead of the existing practice of using December month index only.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Monitoring of Central schemes
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Ministry has any mechanism for monitoring various Central schemes to see whether these schemes are being properly implemented in rural areas of the country; and <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the methodology of this monitoring and cases of lapses noticed during the last two years, State-wise?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):  The Ministry of Rural Development, inter alia, is implementing Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), Deen Dayal Upadhyay – Gramin Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY),  Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana – Gramin (PMAY-G), Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) and National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP)  to bring about overall improvement in the quality of life of the people in rural areas through employment generation, strengthening of livelihood opportunities, promoting self-employment, skilling of rural youths, provision of social assistance and other basic amenities. <br/><br/>In order to ensure that the programme benefits reach the rural poor in full measure, the Ministry has evolved a comprehensive multi-level and multi-tool system of monitoring and evaluation of the implementation of rural development programmes, including Performance Review Committee Meetings, District Development Co-ordination and Monitoring Committee named as “DISHA”, National Level Monitors, Area Officers Schemes, Common Review Mission (CRM), Concurrent Evaluation and Impact Assessment Studies. <br/><br/>As per the reports/returns received from the state governments/UT Administrations, the implementation of these programmes have been found to be satisfactory. Independent studies have also observed positive socio-economic impacts of rural development programmes in rural areas. <br/><br/><br/>*****<br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Crash of ONGC helicopters ferrying officers from Mumbai
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the number of helicopters which crashed in recent years carrying ONGC officers from Mumbai;<br/>(b) the number of officers who died therein; and<br/>(c) the company to which these helicopters belonged and the facts which came forth in investigation reports thereon?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF PETROLEUM & NATURAL GAS <br/>                                     (SHRI DHARAMENDRA PRADHAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c). A Pawan Hans Helicopter operative under contract with ONGC had crashed in the Arabian Sea on 13th January, 2018, while carrying five ONGC officers on board from Juhu Helibase, Mumbai to Mumbai Offshore. All five ONGC officials onboard died in the crash. Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under Ministry of Civil Aviation is investigating the helicopter accident as per the Aircraft (Investigation of Accidents and Incidents) Rules 2017. <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Benefits for migrant construction workers
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)whether it is a fact that under the labour laws, migrant construction workers are entitled to housing and other social security benefits apart from minimum wages, overtime payments and weekly offs;<br/>(b)if so, the measures that have been taken in the last three years to ensure that these benefits are extended to migrant construction workers;<br/>(c)whether any action has been taken against erring construction companies in the last three years in this regard;<br/>(d)if so, the details in this regard; and<br/>(e)whether there is any fund exclusively available for construction workers?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE(IC) FOR LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT<br/>(SHRI SANTOSH KUMAR GANGWAR)<br/><br/>(a) & (b): The construction workers including migrant construction workers are eligible for benefits under various labour laws including the Minimum Wages Act and the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 depending upon their eligibility.  The BOCW Act provides for loans and advances to a beneficiary for construction of a house. <br/>The States are mandated to utilize the cess fund for the welfare of the BOC workers including migrant construction workers in terms of Section 22(1) of the Act and as such the States have formulated various welfare schemes relating to BOC workers life and disability cover, health and maternity benefits, funeral assistance etc.<br/>Contd..2/-<br/>::  2  ::<br/><br/>(c) & (d):	 The office of the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) conducts regular inspection of the construction establishments falling under the Central Sphere to ensure the compliance of the Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996.  Details of Inspections and action taken during the last three years have been mentioned in Annexure. <br/><br/>(e):		 The Building and Other Construction Workers’ (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996 provides for constitution of the Building and Other Construction Workers’ Welfare Fund exclusively for the Building and Other Construction Workers.   The source of the fund is the collection of cess @1% of the cost of construction incurred by the employer under the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Cess Act, 1996.<br/>*                                                *******<br/>

records.qtitle: Bank scam under CBI investigation
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: a)	the names of the banks and total numbers of cases of Bank scam involving more than ? 1000 crore which are under CBI investigation;<br/><br/>b)	for how many years these investigations are going on; and<br/><br/>c)	the name of the banks along with the number of senior officers who are under CBI investigation, the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/>(a) to (c):Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has informed that:<br/><br/>•	As on date 10 cases involving bank fraud amount of Rs. 1000 crore and above pertaining to the following banks are under investigation:<br/><br/>(1) Punjab National Bank (2) Andhra Bank (3) Bank of Baroda (4) SBI (5) Syndicate Bank (6) Canara Bank (7) Corporation Bank (8) Indian Overseas Bank (9) Dena Bank (10) State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur (11) State Bank of Hyderabad (12) State Bank of Patiala (13) Bank of India (14) IDBI Bank (15) State Bank of Travancore (16) State Bank of Mysore (17) Allahabad Bank (18) Bank of Maharashtra (19) Central Bank of India (20) UCO Bank (21) Union Bank of India (22) Exim Bank (23) Dhanlaxmi Bank (24) Axis Bank (25) Karnataka Bank (26) The South Indian Bank (27) Laxmi Vilas Bank.<br/><br/>•	2 cases involving bank fraud amount of Rs. 1000 crore and above pertaining to the IDBI Bank and Canara Bank are also under further investigation after filing of charge-sheets in these cases in the court of law. <br/><br/>•	Year- wise details of cases of pending under investigation is as under:<br/><br/><br/>Year	Number of cases under investigation<br/>2014	1<br/>2015	1<br/>2016	5<br/>2017	2<br/>2018	3<br/><br/>•	10 Bank officers are under CBI investigation in 5 cases. In 7 cases, no Bank officers have been named as accused in the FIR. However, complicity of Bank officers is being looked into during the course of investigation. <br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Transfer policy in banks
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: <br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that in most of the bank frauds, there is involvement of senior bank officials;<br/><br/>(b) whether there is any transfer policy being followed by banks;<br/><br/>(c) the total period of stay allowed to an employee or an officer in one branch of a bank; and<br/><br/>(d) whether Government will ask banks to transfer employees who are staying in a bank branch for more than the allowed period?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a):Reserve Bank of India (RBI)Master Direction on Frauds – Classification and Reporting by commercial banks and select Financial Institutions, provides for banks to complete staff accountability exercise within 6 months from the date of classification of fraud.<br/>Banks examine staff involvement and accountability in all cases of irregularities and on completion of investigation, commensurate punishment is awarded to the delinquent employees based on the seriousness of the wrongdoings as per Bank’s disciplinary rules.<br/>(b) to (d): As per instructions of Central Vigilance Commission, Public Sector Banks (PSBs) are required to identify sensitive posts and to follow a rotation policy in respect of such posts.<br/><br/>Further, RBI, in the context of prevention of frauds, has advised banks to put in place “staff rotation policy” and “policy for mandatory leave for staff”.<br/><br/><br/>Government has also conveyed to PSBs that they should have their own objective, well laid-out transfer and posting rules, which should be followed strictly. Government has further conveyed that all decisions should be taken based on facts of the case and objectivity, and no such decision should be taken for any extraneous consideration.    <br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Roads to connect rural habitations
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government has any plan to construct roads to connect rural habitations in the country; <br/><br/>(b) 	if so, the total length of roads built and the number of rural habitations connected; and <br/><br/>(c) 	the names of States that have benefited most and the least, with a particular reference to Bihar and Jharkhand?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI RAM KRIPAL YADAV)<br/><br/>(a)	:	As per Pradhan Mantri Gram SadakYojana(PMGSY)guidelines, only unconnected rural habitations having population of 500 persons and above (Census 2001) in Plain areas and 250 persons and above (Census 2001) in Special Category States  (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir and Uttarakhand), the desert Areas (as identified in the Desert Development Programme), the Tribal (Schedule V) areas and selected Tribal and Backward Districts (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Planning Commission) are eligible for a single connectivity through an all whether road under PMGSY.<br/><br/>For most intensive LWE blocks as identified by Ministry of Home Affairs the unconnected habitations with population 100 and above (as per 2001 Census) are eligible under PMGSY.<br/><br/>(b)	:	Under PMGSY, 5,34,734.15 km road length has been constructed and 1,45,035 habitations have been connected till date including those habitations connected through other State Schemes.<br/><br/>(c)	:	The details of length(km) of PMGSY roads sanctioned and constructed with respect to the States including Bihar and Jharkhand is given in Annexure.<br/><br/>***** <br/> <br/>

records.qtitle: Road safety norms for private taxi operating companies
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has any proposal to join hands with private-taxi operating companies to create awareness about road safety among road users;<br/><br/> (b) whether Government would impress upon these companies to ask their drivers to follow road safety norms strictly and set example for other road users; and<br/><br/> (c) if so, the details in this regard?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE  MINISTER OF STATE  IN THE  MINISTRY  OF  ROAD  TRANSPORT  AND HIGHWAYS<br/>(SHRI  MANSUKH  L. MANDAVIYA)<br/><br/>(a)	No such proposal is under consideration of Ministry of Road Transport & Highways.  <br/><br/>(b) & (c)  The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways administer Motor Vehicles (MV) Act 1988 and Central Motor Vehicle Rules (CMVR) 1989. However, its provisions are enforced by the States / UTs. The Ministry has been issuing advisories to the States / UTs from time to time for strict enforcement of provisions of MV Act 1988 and CMVR 1989. <br/>	Further the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has been undertaking various publicity measures in the form of telecasting/broadcasting of T.V. spots/Radio jingles, display of cinema slides, etc. containing road safety messages to create awareness about road safety among various segments of road users including drivers. <br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Defence manufacturing under Make in India
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether Government has received any proposals from any State Government for promoting defence manufacturing under ‘Make in India’ programme; and<br/><br/>(b) if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF DEFENCE<br/>DR. SUBHASH BHAMRE<br/><br/><br/>(a) & (b):  Yes, Sir.  In the Budget Speech of 2018-19, Government has announced setting up of two Defence Industrial Corridors for promoting defence manufacturing under ‘Make in India’ initiative of the Government.  Subsequent to the announcement, Government has received three proposals from the States of Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Telangana.  Out of these three States, Government has decided to set up two Defence Industrial Corridors, one in the State of Tamil Nadu and the other in States of Uttar Pradesh.  These are spanning across Chennai, Hosur, Coimbatore, Salem and Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu and spanning across Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Kanpur and Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh (UP).<br/><br/>         In addition, a proposal from Government of Punjab was also received for setting up Light Combat Vehicle (LCV) manufacturing unit in the State of Punjab.  However, the proposal of setting up of manufacturing unit in the Government / Public sector was not found to be a viable proposition at that stage.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Reach of PDS in backward areas
records.name: Harivansh
records.min_name: CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry has been reviewing the Public Distribution System (PDS) in the backward districts of the country;<br/>(b) if so, the details thereof and the number of such districts identified in Bihar; and<br/>(c) the other steps taken to ensure that PDS reaches the deprived and backward areas?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD & PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION<br/>(SHRI RAMVILAS PASWAN)<br/>(a) to (c): NITI Ayog has identified 115 districts, which have shown relatively less progress in achieving key social outcomes especially in Health & Nutrition, Education and Basic Infrastructure. These districts are termed as ‘aspirational districts’, and 13 of such districts are in Bihar.<br/>Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) is operated under the joint responsibility of the Central and State Governments/Union Territories (UTs) Administrations. Central Government is responsible for procurement, State/UT-wise allocation and transportation of foodgrains upto the designated depots of the Food Corporation of India for each State/UT. The operational responsibilities for distribution of foodgrains, within the State/UT, including identification of eligible households, issuance of ration cards to them, delivery of foodgrains upto door-steps of fair price shops (FPS), its distribution through FPSs and supervision over and monitoring of functioning of FPS, etc. rest with the concerned State/UT Government.<br/>Central Government reviews implementation of TPDS in States/UTs, through meetings with them at various levels and video conferencing. Central Government also assists State Governments in the foodgrains distribution process under TPDS by providing financial assistance for meeting expenditure on intra-State movement & handling of foodgrains and FPS dealers’ margin.<br/>***

records.qtitle: Complaints of leakage and poor quality of food in Anganwadis
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the Ministry has decided not to offer money to beneficiaries in place of take home rations provided in Anganwadis; and<br/><br/>(b)	if so, what steps are being taken or have been taken to deal with the complaints of leakages, poor quality of food supplements and involvement of vested interests under this scheme?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI MANEKA SANJAY GANDHI)<br/><br/><br/>(a) 	to (b):   A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PART (A) TO (B) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 299 FOR 22.03.2018 BY SHRI HARIVANSH REGARDING “COMPLAINTS OF LEAKAGE AND POOR QUALITY OF FOOD IN ANGANWADIS”.<br/><br/><br/><br/>(a)	Yes Sir, the Ministry has decided not to offer money to beneficiaries in place of take home rations provided in Anganwadis.<br/><br/>(b)	Supplementary Nutrition (SN) is one of the six services provided at the Anganwadi Centres under the Anganwadi Services of Umbrella ICDS Scheme.  The States/UTs are responsible to implement the Scheme including management, control and distribution of Supplementary Nutrition.  Government of India issue guidelines; releases its share of funds and monitors the scheme.  Whenever any complaint about leakages, poor quality of food supplements of Supplementary Nutrition or any issue connected therewith is received, the same is forwarded to the States/UTs for rectification/action.  A report on complaints containing serious allegations is sought by the Ministry.<br/><br/>Government has introduced 5-tier monitoring and review mechanism at different levels (National/ State/ District/ Block and Village level) for monitoring the status of Anganwadi Centres. Government has issued guidelines on 31.03.2011 for Constitution of Monitoring and Review Committees at different levels to review progress in implementation of the Anganwadi Services Scheme. Composition and key roles of such committees at different levels have been defined and with a view to strengthen and make the scheme more participatory, Panchayati Raj institutions and MPs and MLAs have been assigned representation on various committees at State, District and Block level Monitoring Committees. <br/><br/>Besides the in-built five-tier monitoring system, the newly set up POSHAN Mission has ICT-based real-time monitoring system through Common Application Software (CAS). To digitize and computerize the data generated at the AWCs, Tablets and Smart Phones are provided to Lady Supervisors and Anganwadi workers.<br/>			<br/><br/>********<br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Modernisation and expansion plan of SAIL
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that a huge amount has been spent so far by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) on modernisation and expansion programmes of its projects;<br/><br/>(b)	if so, the names of these plants where the SAIL has undertaken the expansion and modernisation programme; and<br/><br/>(c)	whether this effort has achieved any success in the last three years?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR STEEL		       (SHRI VISHNU DEO SAI)<br/><br/>(a)&(b): Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) had undertaken modernization and expansion of its five integrated steel plants at Bhilai (Chhatisgarh), Bokaro (Jharkhand), Rourkela (Odisha), Durgapur (West Bengal) &  Burnpur (West Bengal) and Special Steel Plant at Salem (Tamil Nadu) to enhance its crude steel production capacity from 12.8 Million tonnes per annum (Mtpa) to 21.4 Mtpa. The cumulative expenditure incurred till January, 2018 is Rs.67,081 crore towards modernisation and expansion, mines and related sustenance schemes.<br/><br/>(c)	The Modernisation and Expansion Plan at Rourkela, IISCO Burnpur, Durgapur, Bokaro and Salem Steel Plants have been completed. The Expansion Plan of SAIL, besides capacity enhancement, adequately addresses the need of SAIL Plants towards eliminating technological obsolescence, energy savings, enriching product mix, pollution control, developing mines & collieries to meet higher requirement of key inputs, introduce customer centric processes and have matching infrastructure facilities in the Plant to support higher production volumes.<br/><br/>********<br/>

records.qtitle: Under five mortality rate
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a) whether it is a fact that the number of annual under five deaths in India has gone down for the first time in 2016;<br/><br/>(b) if so, the number for the years 2014 and 2015 as compared to 2016;<br/><br/>(c) the steps taken to prevent higher mortality among girls as compared to boys; and<br/><br/>(d) the plans of Government to meet its Millennium Development Goal target for the under-five mortality rate of 25 per 1000 live births by 2030?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER<br/>THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND <br/>FAMILY WELFARE<br/>(SHRI ASHWINI KUMAR CHOUBEY)<br/>(a) & (b):	As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) report – 2016 of Registrar General of India, the Under-five Mortality Rate (U5MR) at national level is 39 per 1,000 live births in  comparison to 43 per 1,000 live births in 2015 and 45 per 1,000 live births in 2014.<br/><br/>(c) & (d):	All the programmes/ Schemes under National Health Mission are being implemented universally without any gender based discrimination to reduce Under-five Mortality Rate and to achieve Sustainable Development Goals target of U5MR of 25 per 1000 live births by 2030. These are as below:<br/><br/>(1)	Promotion of Institutional deliveries through cash incentive under JananiSurakshaYojana (JSY) and JananiShishuSurakshaKaryakaram (JSSK) which entitles all pregnant women delivering in public health institutions to absolutely free ante-natal check-ups, delivery including Caesarean section, post-natal care and treatment of sick infants till one year of age.<br/><br/>(2)	Strengthening of delivery points for providing comprehensive and quality Reproductive, Maternal, New-born, Child and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A) Services, ensuring essential new-born care at all delivery points, establishment of Special New-born Care Units (SNCU), New-born Stabilization Units (NBSU) and Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) units for care of sick and small babies. Home Based New-born Care (HBNC) is being provided by ASHAs to improve child rearing practices. India New-born Action Plan (INAP) was launched in 2014 to make concerted efforts towards attainment of the goals of “Single Digit Neonatal Mortality Rate” and “Single Digit Stillbirth Rate”, by 2030.<br/><br/>(3)	Early initiation and exclusive breastfeeding for first six months and appropriate Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices are promoted in convergence with Ministry of Women and Child Development. Village Health and Nutrition Days (VHNDs) are observed for provision of maternal and child health  services and creating awareness on maternal and child care including health and nutrition education. Mothers’ Absolute Affection (MAA) programme for improving breastfeeding practices (Initial Breastfeeding within one hour, Exclusive Breastfeeding up to six months and complementary feeding up to two years) through mass media campaigns and capacity building of health care providers in health facilities as well as in communities. <br/><br/>(4)	Universal Immunization Programme (UIP) is being supported to provide vaccination to children against many life threatening diseases such as Tuberculosis, Diphtheria, Pertussis, Polio, Tetanus, Hepatitis B and Measles. “Mission Indradhanush and Intensified Mission Indradhanush” was launched to fully immunize children who are either unvaccinated or partially vaccinated; those that have not been covered during the rounds of routine immunization for various reasons. Measles Rubella Campaign is being undertaken in select States for children from 9 months to 15 years of age with the aim of eliminating Measles by 2020.<br/><br/>(5)	Name based tracking of mothers and children till two years of age (Mother and Child Tracking System) is done to ensure complete antenatal, intranatal, postnatal care and complete immunization as per schedule.<br/><br/>(6)	Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) for health screening, early detection of birth defects, diseases, deficiencies, development delays including disability and early intervention services has been Operationalized to provide comprehensive care to all the children in the age group of 0-18 years in the community.<br/><br/>(7)	Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres (NRCs) have been set up at public health facilities to treat and manage the children with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) admitted with medical complications.<br/><br/>(8)	Some other important interventions are Iron and folic acid (IFA) supplementation for the prevention of anaemia among the vulnerable age groups, home visits by ASHAs to promote exclusive breast feeding and promote use of ORS and Zinc for management of diarrhoea in children.<br/><br/>(9)	Health and nutrition education through Information, Education & Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) to promote healthy practices and create awareness to generate demand and improve service uptake.<br/><br/><br/>(10)	Capacity building of health care providers: Various trainings are being conducted under National Health Mission (NHM) to build and upgrade the skills of health care providers in basic and comprehensive obstetric care of mother during pregnancy, delivery and essential new-born care.<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>

records.qtitle: (clubbed) Increase in wilful defaulters in PSBs
records.name: Sanjay Sinh
records.qn_text: a)	whether it is a fact that wilful defaulters in PSU banks have risen in the last three years;<br/>b)	if so, the details thereof;<br/>c)	the details of lending of corporate and multinational sectors in the country which accounted for NPA in domestic sector for Indian Banks; and<br/>d)	action taken by Government apart from filing cases to recover the bad loans, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE<br/><br/><br/>(a) and (b): As per data reported by Public Sector Banks, the total number of wilful defaulters has grown from 6,336 as on 31.3.2014, to 9,063 as on 31.12.2017.<br/><br/>(c): As per Reserve Bank of India data on domestic operations, the aggregate Corporate Lending Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) of Scheduled Commercial Banks were Rs. 1,94,621 crore, as on 31.3.2015, and increased to Rs. 6,63,877 crore, as on 31.12.2017 (provisional data).<br/><br/>(d): Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 has been enacted for time-bound resolution of stressed assets. Further, the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 has been amended last year to provide for authorisation by the Government to RBI, for issuing directions to banks to initiate the insolvency resolution process under the Code. Under the provisions of this amending legislation, RBI has issued directions to certain banks for referring 12 accounts, with outstanding amounts greater than Rs. 5,000 crore and with 60% or more classified as non-performing as of 31.3.2016, to initiate insolvency process under the Code. In accordance with these directions, banks have filed applications in respect of these accounts before the National Company Law Tribunal. Further, keeping in view the enactment of the Code, RBI has recently issued a revised framework for resolution of stressed assets, which provides for time-bound resolution of high-value stressed accounts, requiring filing of insolvency application under the Code in case of non-implementation of Resolution Plan within 180 days.<br/>Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest has been amended in 2016 to make it more effective. Further, six new Debts Recovery Tribunals have been established to expedite recovery.<br/><br/>In addition, under the Public Sector Banks (PSBs) Reforms Agenda, PSBs have committed, inter-alia, to ensure Stressed Asset Management verticals for stringent recovery.<br/>***<br/> <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Committee for review of capital acquisition projects

records.qtitle: Measures for improving welfare of wildlife
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is fact that the Ministry has decided to adopt a mechanism under which organizations and companies implementing projects in and around national parks and wildlife sanctuaries have to submit an annual compliance report for the welfare of wildlife;<br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof with particular reference to the welfare of wildlife in those forests where road projects are being implemented or where roads are already exists; and<br/>(c)	steps taken to ensure that wild animals are not killed due to rash and negligent driving on these roads?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/><br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a), (b) & (c)	The Standing Committee of National Board for Wildlife in its 47th meeting held on 25th January, 2018 decided that the user agencies should submit the annual report on compliance of the conditions stipulated in approvals granted under Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 to the States Chief Wildlife Warden for the protection of wildlife.<br/><br/>Wildlife Institute of India (WII) of the Ministry has written guidelines on the Eco-friendly Measures to Mitigate Impacts of Linear Infrastructures on Wildlife. These guidelines provide standard template on structural and non-structural measures for mitigating the impact of roads, railway lines and power lines on wildlife including birds.<br/><br/>The Standing Committee of National Board for Wildlife considers and recommends the developmental activities / projects inside the Protected Areas along with the site specific conditions and mitigation measures imposed by the State Chief Wildlife Warden, State Board for Wildlife, National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India to safeguard the wildlife. <br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Development of GM mustard
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the total amount spent by National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) so far on the development of hybrid/GM mustard;<br/><br/>(b)	whether it is fact that the hybrid DMH4 showed great potential;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, whether the commercialization of it has been given to a private company by NDDB;<br/><br/>(d)	the process of selection of the company and how much royalty/fees has been received so far; and<br/><br/>(e)	whether Government is aware of any conflict of interest issues in the decision to give the commercialization exclusively to a private company?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE (SHRI GAJENDRA SINGH SHEKHAWAT)<br/><br/><br/>(a)	As per the information received from National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), NDDB either directly or through its subsidiaries funded the Rapeseed-Mustard research project at University of Delhi (1995- September 2016) and Nagpur University (1992-2017). Under these projects NDDB had incurred total expenditure of Rs 54.05 crores from 1992- June 2017.<br/><br/>(b)	DMH 4 was evaluated in Initial Hybrid Trials under All India Coordinated Research Project on Rapeseed Mustard during 2013 in Zone II (North Western Plain Zone) and Zone III (Central India). In Zone- II, DMH 4 was found superior over checks NRCHB 506 (+13.41%), NRCDR 02 (+12.80%), Kranti (+18.27) and lesser to check DMH1 (-1.5%). In Zone-III, DMH 4 was found superior over checks NRCHB 506 (+8.65%), RGN-73 (+5.69%) and DMH1 (+ 8.87%).<br/><br/>(c)	Yes, as per the information received from NDDB, NDDB has given license under a License Agreement on ''First Right Basis'' for a period of five years to Metahelix Life Sciences Ltd., Bangalore and its affiliates for production and marketing of DHM-4 for the purpose of its wider spread and commercial cultivation by farmers.<br/><br/>(d)	The NDDB has informed that the Management Committee for the Research Project on Rapeseed Mustard, which included representatives from Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and University of Delhi South Campus approved the commercialization of the DMH 4 through Metahelix Life Sciences Private Limited, Bangalore. As the cultivation of these hybrids required significant extension work in terms of educating farmers on the package of practices to be followed, private seed companies argued that unless exclusivity is provided it would be difficult for them to invest in the business. Under the License Agreement, NDDB has received royalty of Rs 7.91 lakhs for the years 2015-16 and 2016-17.<br/><br/>(e)	ICAR is not aware of any conflict of interest issue.<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Making textbooks thinner and school bags lighter
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the Curriculum Committee of the NCERT has decided to make textbooks thinner and school bags lighter, in order to reduce the workload on students; <br/><br/>(b)	whether any steps have been taken to devise a mechanism to standardise the quality of textbooks in the country during the last one year;<br/><br/>(c)	if so, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(d)	what measures have been taken to evaluate the quality of textbooks of private publishers in the country?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (d)	A statement is laid on the Table of the House.	<br/><br/>STATEMENT REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (a) to (d) OF RAJYA SABHA STARRED QUESTION NO. 215 TO BE ANSWERED ON 15.03.2018 ASKED BY SHRI HARIVANSH, MP REGARDING ‘MAKING TEXTBOOKS THINNER AND SCHOOL BAGS LIGHTER’.<br/><br/>(a)	The purpose of education is to bring out a good human being out of the system. For real development along with knowledge, Life Skill education, value education, physical education, experiential learning is essential. Creative skills need to be nurtured. It was demand from all stakeholders that because of heavy curriculum, there is no time left for all these aspects. Also rote learning is not the way forward. Therefore, School Syllabus must be rationalized. To achieve this, the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has been advised to undertake an exercise to review its syllabus with a view to reducing the curriculum load on the students.  They have conducted a workshop in this regard and have come out with following plan of action for reducing the Curriculum burden:  <br/><br/>1.	Analysis of NCERT’s syllabi and textbooks across subject areas and classes focusing on the following:<br/><br/>a.	Learning outcomes.<br/>b.	Curriculum linkages across classes and subjects<br/>c.	Overlapping in the content (science and geography; physics and chemistry, etc.)<br/>d.	Comprehensibility of language<br/>e.	Age-appropriateness of the content<br/>f.	Diverse contexts<br/><br/>2.	Inviting suggestions from teachers, students, parents and other stake holders through web portal on the reduction of curriculum load. <br/><br/>3.	Developing framework for Experiential Learning through mapping of curricular concepts, life skills and values for holistic development of children. <br/><br/>Suggestions have been invited from various stakeholders through the website of the Ministry of Human Resource Development (MHRD) on 05.03.2018.  The suggestions can be made till April 6th, 2018.  NCERT has also placed an advertisement in the newspapers informing the stakeholders about the MHRD’s website for sending their suggestions on rationalizing curriculum burden.<br/><br/>(b) & (c)	The National Curriculum Framework (NCF) 2005 developed by the NCERT, as per the mandate of the National Policy on Education 1986 (as modified in 1992), sets the guidelines and direction for the development of syllabi and textbooks at all the school stages. The NCERT has developed model textbooks for all subjects at all stages of school education in consonance with the principles of NCF, 2005.   The NCERT’s textbooks are developed by following a very rigorous procedure.  The State/Union Territory Governments either adopt or adapt the NCERT model text books or develop their own text books based on the NCF.   NCERT also analyzes and reviews the textbooks and other teaching materials prepared by the State Governments.  However, education, being a subject in the Concurrent list of the Constitution and a substantial majority of schools being under the jurisdiction of the State/UT Governments, it for the respective State/UT Governments to ensure the quality of the text books for their schools.  <br/><br/>(d)	There are a number of agencies including the private organizations, which are developing various kind of material in the form of textbooks, guidebooks, teaching support material, question banks, assessment material for children as well as for teachers, both in print and digital mode.  It has not been found feasible to evaluate all the material developed by the private agencies.  NCERT has, however, developed evaluation tools for assessment of quality of e-contents. Any agency/individuals may use this evaluation tool available on http://www.ciet.nic.in/Econtent_Evaluation.php. NCERT has been imparting training to the stakeholders (SCERTs, SIETs, School Boards, DIETs, CTEs faculties and school teachers) for creation and evaluation of e-contents in multiple languages. NCERT has taken adequate steps for development of quality e-contents covering syllabus and textbooks of all classes (I to XII).<br/><br/>**** <br/>

records.qtitle: National Sports Centres for Divyangjan
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether the Ministry has any plans for setting up of the National Sports Centres for Divyangjan; <br/>(b) if so, the details thereof; <br/>(c) whether any financial assistance has been provided to Blind World Cup winning Indian Team;<br/>(d) if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(e) the other steps being taken to encourage sports among disabled persons at various levels?<br/>
records.ans_text: Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment<br/><br/>(SHRI KRISHAN PAL GURJAR)<br/><br/>(a) & (b) - Yes Sir.  The Ministry proposes to establish three (3) Centres of Disability Sports at Zirakpur in Punjab, Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh and Visakhapatnam in  Andhra Pradesh. The  proposed centres shall be state of the art international level centres of excellence in sports for  persons with disabilities with the objective of providing them  the training facilities at par with the latest in the world, thereby enabling  them to effectively compete and win medals in various national and international events. <br/><br/>(c)  & (d) – Yes Sir. Under Awareness Generation and Publicity ( AGP) Scheme of the Ministry, cash award of Rs. 2.00  lakhs has been given to each player of the  Indian Cricket Team for winning 5th Blind Cricket World Cup held at Sharjah, UAE during 8th  to 20th January, 2018. A total amount of  Rs.34.00 lakh was given to 17 players. <br/><br/>(e) - To encourage sports among Persons with Disabilities, the Ministry felicitated    Rio Paralympics medalists, members of T-20 Asia Cup Indian Blind Cricket Team and  Indian Blind Para & Para Judo Teams. Cash awards were distributed under Awareness Generation and Publicity Scheme.  In addition, a  provision has also been made in the Scheme for Implementation of Rights of Persons with Disabilities  Act, 2016 ( SIPDA) for support to sporting events at National/ State  Level. Grants in aid are also released under SIPDA for making sports centres of Sports Authority of India (SAI) accessible for  Divyang Sports persons.<br/><br/>*****<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Taking up Mansarovar Yatra with China
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether it is a fact that the Minister had taken up the issue of Manasarovar Yatra through Nathu La with Chinese Foreign Minister when he was in Delhi in December, 2017; and <br/><br/>(b)	if so, the details thereof particularly with respect to the response of China in this regard? <br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTER OF EXTERNAL AFFAIRS<br/>[GEN. (DR) V. K. SINGH (RETD)]<br/><br/>(a) & (b)	The Kailash Manasarovar Yatra via the Nathu La route was not undertaken in 2017 after the Chinese side cited unfavourable conditions to ensure the safe and smooth conduct of the Yatra on this route.  This matter was raised by the External Affairs Minister with the Chinese Foreign Minister during the latter’s visit to India in December 2017. Subsequently, the Chinese Government has confirmed resumption of Yatra on this route. <br/>
