records.qtitle: Pace of construction of roads
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the length of roads, in kilometers, being constructed at present as Government had promised to construct 30 km roads, daily;<br/><br/>(b)	the percentage escalation in the cost of these projects due to delay in their construction;<br/><br/>(c)	whether Government is considering any other scheme to complete the 	construction of roads at the earliest; and <br/><br/>(d)	whether Government is considering imposing fines on road construction companies responsible for delays?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/><br/>(a) 	The average highways construction is 13.51 km per day till October, 2015.  <br/><br/>(b)	 In item rate contracts, there is a provision for payment of escalation due to delay if it is not attributable to Contractor and percentage escalation in the cost varies from project to project. <br/><br/> (c) 	No, Sir. Regular Meetings of Infrastructure Committee headed by Minister for Shipping, Road Transport & Highways are being taken for removing the obstruction like land acquisition, utility shifting, non-availability of soil/aggregate,  environment/forest/wildlife clearances, ROB & RUB issues with Railways, etc. for earliest construction of roads.<br/><br/>(d) 	Suitable action is taken as per the contractual provisions against the Contractor responsible for delay. <br/><br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Hike in electricity tariffs
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether Government is contemplating to increase electricity tariffs after having consultations with the States;<br/><br/>(b) 	the new policy of Government to gradually increase electricity tariffs;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the likely impact of increase in electricity tariffs on common men has been looked into; and<br/><br/>(d) 	whether Government is considering to provide financial help to the States to bail out the State Electricity Boards?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER, <br/>COAL AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY<br/><br/>( SHRI  PIYUSH GOYAL )<br/> <br/>(a) & (b):  	Tariff of distribution companies is determined by the State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs)/Joint Electricity Regulatory Commissions (JERCs) based on the principles enunciated under the Electricity Act, 2003 and policies framed thereunder. There is no provision for direct regulation of the electricity tariff by the Central Government. <br/><br/>(c) :		Through appropriate policy framework and programmes, the Government is promoting efficiency in generation, transmission and distribution business as also supporting strengthening of the distribution and transmission infrastructure, with a view to reducing the Aggregate Technical and Commercial (AT&C) losses. These measures, along with the Government’s emphasis on discovery of tariff through competitive bidding, contribute towards lowering of tariff rates. <br/><br/>(d) :		Ministry of Power has launched a Scheme UDAY-Ujwal Discom Assurance Yojana on 20.11.2015. The scheme envisages taking over of DISCOM debt by States outside the fiscal deficit limits leading to reduction in interest burden; reduction in cost of power; priority/additional funding through schemes of Ministry of Power/Ministry of New and Renewable Energy; and measures to prevent future slippages.<br/><br/><br/>*********<br/>

records.qtitle: Implementation of procurement policy for urea and manure
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	the time by which Government proposes to implement procurement policy for urea and manure;<br/><br/>(b) 	the details of the report of Government suggesting the hazards caused from urea consumption;<br/><br/>(c)	the details of the total availability of manures in the country and the steps taken by Government to enhance its production;<br/><br/>(d)	whether natural manure is cheaper than chemicals fertilizers and the steps taken by Government to popularize it; and <br/><br/>(e)	the details of the production of natural manure as on date and how much Government will save by linking it to subsidy?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS<br/><br/>						                       (SHRI HANSRAJ GANGARAM AHIR)<br/>___________________________________________________________<br/><br/>(a):	There is no such policy.  However, as per the extant policy provisions, the import of urea is done through three State Trading Enterprises (STEs) i.e. MMTC Ltd. (MMTC), State Trading Corporation (STC) and Indian Potash Limited (IPL), based on the demand projected by Department of Agriculture, Co-operation and Farmers’ Welfare. <br/><br/>(b):	 No such report came to notice regarding hazards caused from urea consumption.<br/><br/>(c):	 Details of organic manure availability in the country (excluding green manures) is annexed.  Steps taken by Government to enhance its production are as follows: <br/> <br/>i.          To improve the availability of manures in the country  100% assistance to State Government/Government agencies upto a maximum  limit  of  Rs. 190.00 lakh/unit and  33%  of  cost  limited  to Rs. 63 lakh/unit for individuals/private agencies through NABARD as capital investment for 3000 TPA production capacity.<br/><br/>ii.         For promotion of organic inputs on farmers’ field(manure, vermin-compost, bio-fertilizers liquid/solid, waste compost, herbal extracts etc.) there is provision of financial assistance  under Soil Health management component of National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture(NMSA) @ 50% of cost subject to a limit of Rs. 5000/- per ha and Rs. 10,000 per beneficiary. <br/><br/>iii.        There is a provision of financial assistance under Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)  for setting up of vermi-compost units/organic input production unit (size - 30ft x 8ft x 2.5ft) @ Rs.1 lakh per unit for permanent structure and Rs. 16,000/- per unit for HDPE vermin-bed.<br/><br/>(d):	No such cost comparison of chemical fertilizers and organic manure has been done. However, organic manure/compost are produced on-farm by the farmers using the available resources may be cost effective.  Under NMSA, the National Centre of Organic Farming (NCOF), Ghaziabad, is conducting various extension and publicity activities like Exhibitions, Radio Talks, TV Programmes, distribution of literature on organic inputs/ organic farming etc to educate farmers. NCOF is also publishing Bio-Fertilizer News Letter as well as Organic Farming News Letter Bi-annually and Quarterly respectively. In addition, various books on production and use of bio-fertilizers have been published in various languages for distribution to the farming community. Radio jingle (Hindi) on promotion of organic agriculture broadcasted on 4 different FM Radio Stations at Delhi, Bangalore, Nagpur and Lucknow.<br/><br/>(e):	The details of production of natural manure is annexed.  Regarding saving by linking it to subsidy no data is available.<br/><br/>             ******* <br/>

records.qtitle: Lack of co ordination between RBI and GOI
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) Whether there is any difference of opinion between Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Finance on Monetary Policy, Interest-rate and the report of Financial Sector Legislative Reform Commission;<br/><br/>(b) Whether Government proposes to down size the rights of the Reserve Bank of India;<br/><br/>(c) Whether there is lack of co-ordination between the RBI and the policies of Government on economic reforms; and<br/><br/>(d) if so, the extent to which the growth rate is being affected as a result thereof?

records.qtitle: Defence import by the country
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether it is a fact that India’s share has been 15 percent in the global import of weapons during the last five years;<br/><br/>(b) whether 59 percent of the defence budget is spent on the import of weapons; and<br/><br/>(c) the quantum of reduction in the defence import during the last one year; after the concept of Make in India?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF DEFENCE<br/>           (SHRI MANOHAR PARRIKAR)<br/><br/><br/>(a) The information is being collected and will be laid on the Table of the House.<br/><br/>(b) & (c):  The expenditure on capital acquisition in respect of orders placed on Indian vendors and foreign vendors during the period from 2011-12 to 2014-15 was Rs.138630.82 crore (56.02%) and Rs.108852.55 crore (43.98%) respectively. records.qtitle: Auction of completed projects
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the reasons behind Governments intention to auction only completed road projects; <br/><br/>(b) the benefits going to be accrued to Government from this auction process and whether foreign complanies would collect excessive toll tax for their profits; and <br/><br/>(c) whether the Ministry has no scheme for resorting to auction of completed roads only?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI PON. RADHAKRISHNAN)<br/><br/>(a) to (c)	A proposal for monetisation of Highways of completed public funded national highway (NH) projects through Toll-Operate-Transfer (TOT) mode based on the expected collection of user fee receivables, through private sector efficiency & expertise is under active consideration in the Ministry. Proceeds from such monetisation of completed NH projects which shall accrue to the government/authority are to be utilised for construction and operation and maintenance of national highways throughout the country. The user fees shall be collected post auction as per existing provisions of the National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008 and amendments thereof. At present completed public funded national highway (NH) projects are bid out to private developers for operation and maintenance including toll collection for a pre-determined period on Operate-Maintain-Transfer (OMT) mode.<br/><br/><br/>***** <br/>

records.qtitle: Transmission lines affected by land acquisition issues
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	to what extent the construction of transmission lines has been affected due to land acquisition issues;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether information about future problems caused by construction of transmission lines is given to the affected parties before starting construction of these lines;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether the compensation amount would also be provided by companies constructing transmission lines or it would be borne only by the State Governments; and<br/><br/>(d) 	the annual losses being borne by Government in electricity due to faults in transmission lines?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR POWER, <br/>COAL AND NEW & RENEWABLE ENERGY<br/><br/>( SHRI  PIYUSH GOYAL )<br/> <br/>(a) :		As per provisions of existing law, land below transmission line towers is not required to be acquired and the land owner retains the ownership of the land even after the construction of the transmission lines.<br/><br/>(b):		Ttransmission projects, by their inherent nature, have negligible impact on environmental and social attributes, which are confined to Right of Way (RoW). Nevertheless, before construction of any transmission line, general public including persons likely to be affected are informed through a “Public Notice,” which are published in local newspapers giving details of transmission line with its proposed route, name of villages/district(s) etc.<br/> <br/>(c):		Compensation amount is paid by the transmission licensee/implementing agency to the affected land owners according to established procedure and as decided by concerned authorities/District Magistrate(s)as per the extant rules/guidelines. State Government can provide enhanced compensation, if required, to the affected land owner. <br/><br/>(d):		Losses in electricity due to faults in transmission lines is not borne by the Government.<br/><br/>**********<br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Disbursement of loans to youth
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the criteria for disbursement of skill loans to youth amounting to ` 5000-15000, have been fixed; <br/><br/>(b)	whether those youth would be given money for skill development for starting their own business using their skills (entrepreneurship); and <br/><br/>(c)	the role of State Government in this loan?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) 	The Government has launched Skill Loan Scheme on 15th July, 2015 to promote loan facility to individuals who intend to take up skill development courses.  As per criteria of the scheme, any individual who has secured admission in a course in an organization eligible under the scheme, leading to a certificate/diploma/degree issued by such organization as per National Skill Qualification Framework (NSQF) is eligible for a Skill Loan.  The loan range is Rs. 5,000-1,50,000.<br/><br/>(b)  	There is no such provision under the Skill Loan Scheme.<br/><br/>(c) 	While there is no direct role of State Government envisaged under Skill Loan Scheme, however the state governments are expected to mobilize youth to take skill loans to overcome financial difficulties in undergoing skill training programmes.<br/>

records.qtitle: Projects approved for NE region
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	the names of the projects approved for the development of North East in 2014-15 and the names of such projects for which the time limit for approval was 2014-15, whether those projects had been completed, if not, the hindrance therein; <br/>(b) 	the main obstacles in the development of North East, whether those problems have been resolved to some extent during last ten years; and<br/>(c) 	if so, the details of the problems that have been solved and remaining problems that are still persisting?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) IN THE MINISTRY OF DEVELOPMENT OF NORTH EASTERN REGION<br/>( DR. JITENDRA SINGH )<br/><br/>(a)	: The details of projects sanctioned under different schemes of Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region during 2014-15 for development of the North Eastern Region is given at Annexure. The agreed period of completion of these projects are normally three (3) years from the date of sanction.	<br/><br/>(b) & (c) : The main obstacles in the development of North East are hostile and inaccessible terrain, long rainy season and severe winter, short working season, large area remaining snow bound in some of the regions, law & order issues, land acquisition bottlenecks, environmental clearances, low absorption capacity of the states, delay in sanctioning & completion of projects etc. The issues relating to sanctioning & completion of the projects have been resolved to some extent but problems like law & order, land acquisition, environmental clearances that subsist in this eco-sensitive region, and natural disasters are the issues that need to be resolved on a case to case basis and can not entirely be anticipated for planning purposes.<br/>

records.qtitle: Promotion of sports by private and corporate sector
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether the private and thecorporate sectors are coming forward topromote sports in the country;<br/><br/>(b) to what extent the private sector isco-operating in promotion of sports;<br/><br/>(c) the prospective plan of Governmentto provide better sports infrastructure tothe youth in the rural areas;<br/><br/>(d) whether merely including the sportsin school curriculum will improve thecondition of games and sports in thecountry; and<br/><br/>(e) the details of number of schools inthe country wherein the sports'' resourcesare available at present?<br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>FOR YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS<br/>(SHRI SARBANANDA SONOWAL)<br/><br/>(a) & (b):	The Government instituted the National Sports Development Fund (NSDF) in 1998 with a view to mobilizing resources from the Government as well as non-governmental sources including the private/corporate sector and non-resident Indians. The Ministry received contributions from Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI), Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Oil & Natural Gas Commission (ONGC), Jindal Steel & Power Ltd, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Videocon International Ltd, Powergrid Corporation of India, State Bank of India, Jaypee Sports International Limited, India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) etc.<br/><br/>Corporate Sector, both public and private, is involved in a big manner in promotion and development of sports in the country.Corporate houses are associated with the Leagues for various Sports such as Indian Premier League (IPL) for Cricket, Hockey India League for Hockey, Indian Super League for Football, Indian Football League and Pro-Kabaddi League. Corporate Houses are also involved in giving financial support directly to sportspersons and sports academies. <br/><br/>Public Sector Undertakings such as Oil & Natural Gas Commission,   Indian Oil Corporation, Steel Authority of India Limited, Air India and many other PSUs have set up Sports Promotion Boards and are giving financial support as well as employment to sportspersons. <br/><br/>Training to promote rural sports, nationally recognized sports, paralympic sports and Olympic sports have been included in the schedule VII of the Companies Act, 2103, which would allow companies to spend on development of sports from the funds earmarked for Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) related activities.  Inclusion of sports in the CSR activities will give a boost to the promotion and development of sports in the country and the much needed funds from companies, both in public and private sector, will flow to the sports sector.<br/><br/>(c):	For development of sports infrastructure in rural areas, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan (RGKA) a centrally sponsored schemes introduced in 2014-15 in place of erstwhile PYKKA, provides for construction of integrated sports complexes, both for outdoor and indoor sports, in each block of the country, in a phased manner, through convergence of funds from different Schemes of the Government.  <br/><br/>(d):	Mere inclusion of sports in school curriculum is not enough for improving the condition of games and sports. since sports is a state subject, primary responsibility for development and promotion of sports including in schools is that of the State Governments. However, the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports and Sports Authority of India (SAI) supplement the efforts of State Government under its various Schemes such as Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan (RGKA), Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme (USIS), Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs), National Sports Talent Contest (NSTC) Scheme, Army Boys Sports Company (ABSC) Scheme, SAI Training Centres (STC) Scheme, Special Area Games (SAG) Scheme and Centre of Excellence (CoE) Scheme. Further, the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports has recently launched the National Sports Talent Search Scheme (NSTSS) with the objectives of identification of sporting talent among students in the age group of 8-12 years (for admission in Class IV to Class VI) and nurturing of the sporting potential/ talent in District level Sports Schools/ Central Sports Schools/ Junior Sports Academies etc., to make them excel in the National and international sports competitions.<br/><br/>(e):	The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports does not maintain data about the schools having sports resources.<br/><br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Establishment of DMF in Jharkhand
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the total number of districts in Jharkhand where District Mineral Foundation (DMF) has been established; <br/>(b)	the total share from revenue to be given to DMF; <br/>(c)	whether any fund has been given to DMF so far; and <br/>(d)	whether people affected from mining have been given any compensation from DMF and if so, the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: (a): District Mineral Foundation (DMF) is to be established in all the 24 districts of Jharkhand.<br/><br/>(b) & (c): The DMF is to be funded by contributions from holders of mining lease and prospecting licence-cum-mining lease in the following manner:<br/><br/>i.	Contribution from holders of a mining lease or a prospecting licence-cum-mining lease granted on or after the date of commencement of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015 (12.01.2015), which shall be an amount equivalent to such percentage of the royalty as may be prescribed by the Central Government, not exceeding one-third of the royalty.<br/><br/>ii.	Contribution from holders of a mining lease granted before the date of commencement of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2015, which shall be an amount as may be prescribed by the Central Government, not exceeding the amount of the royalty.<br/><br/>The rate of contribution to DMF is required to be decided by the Central Government. As DMFs are yet to be established in the State of Jharkhand, details of funds available with the DMFs or the amount released to DMFs are not available. <br/><br/>(d): Does not arise in view of reply given to (b) and (c) above. <br/><br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Monitoring of assets by Air India to reduce loss
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the plan being made by Government to reduce the operational cost of Air India and to what extent the operational cost of Air India is higher than private airlines;<br/><br/>(b) whether by only selling the assets of Air India, it is possible to take it out of loss;<br/><br/>(c) whether the alternative option of reducing the loss by commercially using their assets has also been contemplated, if so, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d) the steps being taken by Government to bring Air India out of loss?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/><br/>(Dr Mahesh Sharma)<br/><br/>(a) and (d): The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) in its meeting held on 12.04.2012, approved a Turnaround Plan (TAP)/ Financial Restructuring Plan (FRP) for operational and financial turnaround of Air India (AI) subject to achievement of certain laid down milestones by AI. In compliance with TAP/ FRP, an Oversight Committee has been set up under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation with Expenditure Secretary, Additional Secretary and Financial Adviser, Ministry of Civil Aviation, Joint Secretary of Ministry of Civil Aviation and SBI Caps as members, to monitor the Operational and Financial Performance of Air India vis-a-vis the milestones set under TAP/ FRP. So far, eleven meetings of Oversight Committee have been held.<br/><br/>The Company has achieved the Targets set out in the TAP milestones, and has made substantial progress in both Operational as well as Financial Areas. The Operating Loss has consistently reduced and in 2014-15 it is Rs.2171.40 crores (provisional) as compared to Rs.5138.69 crores in 2011-12. The Net Loss is expected to be Rs.5547.40 crores in 2014-15 as against the loss of Rs.7559.74 crores in 2011-12. <br/><br/>As part of the TAP/ FRP, AI has initiated, inter-alia, the following steps in order to cut costs: <br/><br/>i. Rationalization of certain loss making routes<br/><br/>ii. Induction of brand new aircraft on several domestic & international routes to <br/>increase passenger appeal<br/><br/>iii. Phasing out & grounding of old fleet<br/><br/>iv. Establishment of Integrated Operations Control Center and Hub Control Center in Delhi<br/><br/>v. Freezing of employment in non-operational areas<br/><br/>vi. Operationalization of Subsidiary Companies such as Air India Air Transport Services Limited and Air India Engineering Services Limited and transfer of manpower and equipment and treating them as Independent Profit Centers and<br/><br/>vii. Induction of the B787 aircraft on Medium Capacity Long Haul Routes. The comparative statement of the operational cost of Air India viz-a viz the private sector airlines is not maintained in the Ministry.<br/><br/>(b) and (c): As per Turn Around Plan/Financial Restructuring Plan approved by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), Air India is required to monetize its assets and generate Rs.5000 crore over a period of 10 years by way of sale, leasing or developing an asset as a joint venture. Specific approval of the cabinet is necessary for each case of sale or long term lease of land belonging to Govt. or Govt. controlled statutory authorities as per the instructions laid by Ministry of Finance.<br/><br/>Air India is in possession of some properties which are lying vacant and unused for a long time because of shifting of its offices to Airport Terminal Bldg., City location and also as a result of stopping of its operation from such locations etc. Monetizing such properties by way of sale/ rent or to develop as a Joint Venture, to raise Non Operating Revenue, would help the company to retire its huge debts. Government has received proposals for monetisation of following properties from Air India:<br/><br/>1. Residential plot measuring 0.99 acres approx. at Pankaja Mill, Road, Coimbatore<br/><br/>2. Residential cum commercial Plot of Land measuring 1.33 acres approx. at Mount Road, Teynampet, Chennai.<br/><br/>3. 04 nos Flats measuring 2033 sq. ft. approx at Sterling Apartment, Mumbai.<br/><br/>The Government has drafted these proposals for the approval of the Cabinet.<br/>Air India has approached Govt./Public sector undertakings such as Income Tax Deptt., Service Tax Deptt., State Bank of India etc for leasing space in its office building at Nariman Point, Mumbai.The details of earnings of Air India from monetisation of assets are as under:<br/><br/><pre><br/><br/>Year                  Earning<br/>2014-15 -         Rs 35.97. crores<br/>2015-16 -         Rs 90.24 crores ( Prov. Estimates)<br/><br/></pre><br/><br/>The revenue generated from monetisation will be utilized by Air India to reduce its debts, and improve its fiscal health.<br/><br/>                            *****

records.qtitle: Additional allocation of the Ministry

records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE OF PANCHAYATI RAJ<br/>(SHRI NIHAL CHAND)<br/><br/>(a) to (c) An amount of Rs. 94.00 Crores has been allocated to  Ministry of Panchayati Raj as Budget Estimate (BE) for 2015-16. records.qtitle: Investment by private sector in Digital India Programme
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of Communications & Information Technology be pleased to state:<br/><br/>(a)	 whether it is a fact that private sector has given an investment assurance of 4.72 lakhs crore during the launch of Digital India week, if so, by when these investment proposals   would materialise;<br/>(b)	 number of youth likely to be employed under this programme; and<br/>(c)	 the scheme of Government to increase export in the field of telecommunication and the manner in which India could become a leading country in the field of hardware.<br/>
records.ans_text: ANSWER <br/><br/>MINISTER FOR COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY<br/>(SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD)<br/><br/>(a)	and (b):  During the Digital India Week Launch, investment assurances of above Rs. 4.5 lakh crores were given by some of the major industrial houses. These investments are expected to generate over 18 lakh jobs.<br/><br/>(c):   (I) The Government has taken the following steps to increase the exports in  telecom sector:<br/><br/>The Telecom Equipment and Services Export Promotion Council (TEPC) has been set up by the Government to promote export of Telecom Equipments and Services. The Council undertakes activities aimed at export promotion such as commissioning of studies to find potential markets, holding of National/International Seminars and facilitating participation of exporters in various overseas exhibitions. <br/><br/>(II) The following initiatives are being taken by Government to promote electronics manufacturing (including telecom products) in the country.<br/><br/>(i)	Promotion of electronics hardware manufacturing is one of the pillars of Digital India campaign of the Government.<br/><br/>(ii)	Modified Special Incentive Package Scheme (M-SIPS) provides financial incentives to offset disability and attract investments in the sector.<br/><br/>(iii)	Policy for providing preference to domestically manufactured electronic products in Government procurement is under implementation.<br/><br/>(iv)	Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC) Scheme provides financial assistance for creating world-class infrastructure for electronics manufacturing units. Telecom products have been notified under the policy.<br/><br/><br/>(v)	Electronic Development Fund (EDF) policy has been approved to support Daughter Funds including Early Stage Angel Funds and Venture Funds in the area of Electronics System Design and Manufacturing, Nano-electronics and IT. The supported Daughter Funds will promote innovation, R&D, product development and within the country.<br/><br/>(vi)	A meeting of State IT Ministers and State Government Officials was held on 26.08.2014 to encourage them to actively promote electronics manufacturing. Several States have shown keen interest.<br/><br/>(vii)	Approvals for all foreign direct investment up-to 100% in the electronic hardware manufacturing sector are under the automatic route.<br/><br/>(viii)Under the Electronics Hardware Technology Park (EHTP) Scheme, approved units are allowed duty free import of goods required by them for carrying on export activities, CST reimbursement and excise duty exemption on procurement of indigenously available goods, as per the Foreign Trade Policy. <br/><br/>(ix)	Government has imposed basic custom duty at 10% on specified telecommunication products that are outside the purview of the information technology agreement (ITA) and has also imposed education cess on imported electronic products to provide parity between domestically produced goods and imported goods.<br/><br/>(x)	In the foreign Trade Policy, 2015-2020, 2%incentives on export of telecom is available for products under the ‘Merchandise Exports from India Scheme’ (MEIS).<br/><br/>(xi)	Two Schemes for skill development of 90,000 and 3,28,000 persons, respectively  in the electronics sector has been approved to provide human resource for the industry. <br/> <br/>(xii)	Government has approved setting up of two semiconductor wafer fabrication (FAB) manufacturing facilities in India.<br/><br/>(xiii)The ‘Scheme to enhance the number of PhDs in the Electronic System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (ITES) sectors has been approved. 3000 PhDs are proposed to be supported under the Scheme.<br/><br/>(xiv)An Electropreneur park providing Incubation for development of ESDM sector which will contribute IP creation and Product Development in the sector.<br/><br/>(xv)	National Centre of Excellence for Technology on Internal Security (NCETIS) is being set up at IIT-Bombay with the objective  to address the internal security needs of the nation on continuous basis by  delivering  technology prototypes required for internal security and to promote domestic industry in internal security. <br/><br/>(xvi)Centre for Excellence on Internet of Things (IoT) is being set up in Bangluru jointly with Nasscom. <br/><br/>(xvii)The Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY) provides funding under several schemes for promotion of R&D, including support for International Patents in Electronics & IT (SIP-EIT); Multiplier Grants Scheme and Scheme for Technology Incubation and Development of Entrepreneurs (TIDE) in the area of Electronics, ICT and Management.<br/><br/>*******<br/>

records.qtitle: Skill Development university in Bihar
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether there is any proposal for establishment of Skill Development University in Bihar, if so, by when, it would be established; <br/><br/>(b) 	whether any negotiation have been held with Bihar Government in this regard; <br/><br/>(c) 	whether adequate resources are available for providing skill development training to thirty crore youths in five years and the expenditure to be incurred on this ; and <br/><br/>(d)	 whether it is proposed to seek collaboration from the private sector also for skill development?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a) & (b)	A committee has been constituted to work out the modalities for setting up of a Skill University in Bihar along with suggesting the initiatives to scale up and synergize the efforts towards skill development of the youth in the region. <br/><br/>(c) & (d)	There are 12,106 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) (Govt.- 2,285 and Private- 9,821) operational under the Directorate General of Training (DGT) which are the primary institutions for skilling in the Country.<br/><br/>           Besides, the Government has setup the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) as a public private partnership entity to promote private training providers to setup Skill Development centres across the country. As on 30th June, 2015, the 211 NSDC affiliated training partners, have 3669 operational training centres, including 745 mobile centres with coverage across the Country.<br/>

records.qtitle: Plan to inter connect the Buddhist circuits
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	the details of growth in the revenue from the foreign tourists in the last one year; <br/>(b) 	the number of people who have been employed in tourism sector in the last one year; <br/>(c) 	the details of increase in the number of tourists visiting Buddhist circuit; and <br/>(d) 	whether Government has any plan to inter-connect the Buddhist circuits, if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE FOR TOURISM (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>(DR. MAHESH SHARMA)<br/><br/>(a):	The Foreign Exchange Earnings (FEEs) through tourism in India during July, 2014 – June, 2015 was Rs.1,24,488 Crore with a growth rate of  8.05% over July, 2013 – June, 2014.<br/><br/>(b):	As per the 2nd Tourism Satellite Account of India - 2009-10 and subsequent estimation, the total employment in the country due to tourism was 67.0 million during 2012-13. This information is not available for 2013-14 and 2014-15.<br/><br/>(c): 	Ministry of Tourism does not compile the exclusive data of domestic and foreign tourists visiting Buddhist sites. However, the number of Domestic and Foreign Tourist Visits to different States/UTs, including the visits to Buddhist sites during 2014 are given in Annexure.<br/><br/>(d): 	The Ministry of Tourism has launched the Swadesh Darshan scheme with a vision to develop theme based tourist circuits on the principles of high tourist value, competitiveness and sustainability in an integrated manner by synergizing efforts to focus on needs and concerns of all stakeholders to enrich tourist experience and enhance employment opportunities. records.qtitle: Jawans of paramilitary forces posted in North Eastern States
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) the total number of jawans of paramilitary forces in the North-Eastern<br/>States;<br/><br/>(b) the details of annual expenditure involved in their posting;<br/><br/>(c) whether Ministry is considering upon withdrawing the paramilitary forces from the peaceful areas of North-East; and<br/><br/>(d) the steps taken by Government for better monitoring of international borders adjoining the North-Eastern States?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS<br/>(SHRI KIREN RIJIJU)<br/><br/>(a) to (c):	The Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) are made available on the request of the State Governments, to assist them in maintaining the public order. The deployment of these forces in the States including North-Eastern States depend upon the overall security scenario and availability of these Forces. The level of deployment of CAPFs in any State is dynamic and undergoes changes depending upon the developing security situation.  <br/><br/>      The level of deployment of CAPFs is not disclosed in the interest of National Security.<br/><br/>(d):  Government has adopted a multi-pronged approach for effective domination  and  to  check  trans-border  crimes  including  smuggling and <br/>….2/-<br/><br/><br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/><br/>R.S. US.Q. NO. 1792  FOR 05.08.2015<br/><br/>infiltration along the International Borders including North-Eastern States of the country.  The steps taken in this regard is as under :-<br/><br/>i)   Effective domination of the borders by the Border guarding Forces (BGFs) through carrying out round the clock surveillance, by patrolling,  nakas (border ambushes).<br/><br/>ii)     The riverine segments of International Borders are being patrolled and dominated with the help of water crafts / speed boats / floating Border Out Posts of BGFs. <br/><br/>iii)     Usages of Hi-Tech Surveillance equipments along with day and night vision devices on borders. <br/><br/>iv)    In order to develop security infrastructure along the International Borders, including North-Eastern States, the Government has sanctioned construction of fence, border roads, floodlights etc. <br/><br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Plans to check food adulteration effectively
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state: <br/><br/>(a) whether Central Government is contemplating to enact such a stringent legislation in view of the Maggi row so that the quality of the food products could be ensured and justice could be done with the consumers, if so,the details thereof; <br/><br/>(b) the number of laboratories available in the country to check the quality of the food products and the number of posts lying vacant therein;<br/><br/>(c) the action taken by Government, so far, against the companies for the poor quality of the food products; and <br/><br/>(d) the total number of cases pending in the country with regard to adulteration of the food products and the plan to check adulteration effectively?<br/>
records.ans_text: (a):  A Committee had been constituted by the Government of India to undertake a comprehensive review of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The Committee has submitted its report to the Department of Health and Family Welfare and, amongst, others, has also made recommendations to provide for harsher punishment to any person who, whether by himself or by any other person on his behalf, adds an adulterant to food to render it injurious for human consumption with an inherent potential to cause his death  or is likely  to cause such harm on his body as would amount to grievous hurt, irrespective of the fact whether it causes actual injury or not.<br/> (b):     The number of such labs are as below :- <br/><br/>(i)		Referral laboratories   	-	12<br/>(ii)		State/Pubic food laboratories	-	72<br/>(iii)		NABL accredited Private laboratories	-	82<br/>	Total	-	166<br/><br/>Number of posts vacant in these labs is not centrally maintained.<br/><br/><br/>-2-<br/>(c) & (d): Company wise information is not centrally maintained; however, as per information made available by the States/UTs, the number  of cases launched (Criminal /Civil) and number  of conviction/penalties  are as under :<br/><br/>Year	Number of Cases Launched Criminal/Civil	Number of Conviction<br/>	Penalties/<br/>Amount raised <br/>2012-13	5840	3175	Rs. 5,24,95,016<br/>2013-14	10235	913	2932/<br/>Rs. 7,29,89,474<br/>2014-15	9230	1355	2682/ Rs.10,64,03,414<br/><br/>The implementation and enforcement of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 rests with State/UT Governments. Random Samples of food items are drawn by the State Food Safety Officers and sent to the laboratories recognized by the FSSAI for analysis. In cases,  where samples are found to be not conforming to the provisions of the Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder, action is taken as per the provisions of the FSS Act.<br/>The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) also regularly takes up issues relating to enforcement of the provisions of the FSS Act and regulations made thereunder with the State/UT authorities, through various communications sent to them and interactions during the meetings of the Central Advisory Committee.<br/>

records.qtitle: Resignations of eminent personalities
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether the resignations of four eminent personalities like Anil Kakodkar during the last eight months have raised questions and whether these persons have resigned under pressure of the Ministry and if not, the reasons for their resignations; <br/><br/>(b) 	whether a pressure was exerted on these persons to submit resignations, so as to appoint preferred persons; <br/><br/>(c) 	the reasons why a probe was not conducted if their activities were suspicious and if an inquiry was conducted, the details thereof; and <br/><br/>(d) 	whether credibility and autonomy of the institution is not impacted due to the resignations of such persons?<br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/>(a) 	: Dr. Anil Kakodkar, Chairperson, BoG, IIT Bombay requested to be relieved from his responsibilities as Chairperson, BOG, IIT Bombay but agreed to continue till end of his tenure, i.e 11.05.2015.  Prof. R.K. Shevgaonkar, Director, IIT Delhi submitted his resignation due to personal reasons.  The Board of Governors of IIT-Delhi desired that in the larger interests of the Institute, Prof. Shevgaonkar should continue as Director, IIT-Delhi.  Thereafter, the Board endorsed the resignation which was accepted w.e.f. 11.06.2015.  Vice Chancellor, University of Hyderabad submitted resignation on personal grounds and demitted office on 28.01.2015.  Vice Chancellor, Assam University submitted that he is unable to continue in the office because of some personal and family considerations and requested to release him from the responsibilities and to treat request as letter of resignation.  Former Director, NCERT, had sought pre-mature repatriation from the post of Director, NCERT on personal grounds.  She was repatriated to her parent office and relieved from NCERT on 20.10.2014.  <br/><br/>(b) & (c): No, Sir.  The resignations were entirely on personal reasons, therefore no inquiry was called for. <br/><br/>(d)	:     No, Sir.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Implementation of recommendations of Bibek Debroy Committee
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: a)  whether it is a fact that a large scale investment is required to be made in Railways and Government is not able to make investment on such a large scale;  <br/><br/>(b)  whether Government is contemplating to withdraw from running Railway schools and hospitals after recommendations of the Bibek Debroy Committee;  <br/><br/>(c) the number of railway projects pending due to delay in land acquisition, the details thereof; and<br/><br/>(d) whether the Committee has recommended that the private sector be allowed to run Railways and if so, whether the private companies will fix railway fares after such a move?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/>(a): Yes, Sir. Large scale investment is required in Railways. Ministry has planned an investment of ? 8.56 lakh crore over next five years.<br/><br/>(b): No such decision has been taken on the said recommendations of the Bibek Debroy Committee.<br/><br/>(c): As per the study carried out in 2014-15, there are a total of seventy three (73) projects which are severely affected due to delay in land acquisition. Thirty eight (38) projects are related to new lines, twenty eight (28) to doubling and seven (07) to gauge conversion.<br/><br/>(d): The committee has recommended concessioning of commercial operations of trains like Rajdhani and Shatabdi with private operator having freedom on pricing of tickets for a portion of the capacity.<br/><br/>***** <br/><br/>

records.qtitle: Amendment in Forest Rights Act
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)whether Government intends to amend the Forest Rights Act in the name of development projects;<br/><br/>(b) if so, whether the consequences thereof have been studied;<br/><br/>(c)the number of the public and private sectors projects pending for environment clearance; and<br/><br/>(d)the scheme launched for development in the tribal areas after enforcement of the Forest Rights Act and the consequences thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE) FOR ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE <br/>(SHRI PRAKASH JAVADEKAR)<br/><br/>(a) & (b)	There is no such proposal to amend the Forest Rights Act in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. The Nodal Ministry for implementation of Forest Rights Act is Ministry of Tribal Affairs.<br/> <br/>(c)	A total of 475 projects, out of which 103 belong to public and 372 to the private sector, are pending for Environmental Clearance.<br/><br/>(d)The National Scheduled Tribes Finance Development Corporation (NSTFDC), an autonomous body under the administrative control of Ministry of Tribal Affairs has launched Tribal Forest Dwellers Empowerment Scheme. This is a new scheme introduced and NSTFDC has requested the State Channelizing Agencies (SCAs) to implement the same.  As on date, sanction for 66 beneficiaries of Rajasthan has been made.<br/><br/>***<br/>

records.qtitle: Action against aviation companies
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) whether any action has, so far, been taken by the Ministry against the<br/>aviation companies which are charging arbitrary fares and if not, the reasons<br/>therefor;<br/>(b) by when a system for monitoring the air fares will be in place;<br/>(c) whether common man are bearing the brunt of the connivance of some<br/>companies; and<br/>(d) whether some days ago the Civil Aviation Ministry had expressed its<br/>dissent to fix the airfare and if so, the reasons for considering this now by the<br/>Ministry?
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CIVIL AVIATION<br/><br/>(Dr Mahesh Sharma)<br/><br/>(a) to (d) Air fares are not regulated by the Governments. Under the provision of Sub Rule (1) of Rule 135, aircraft Rules 1937, airlines are free to fix<br/>reasonable tariff having regard to all relevant factors, including the cost of operation, characteristics of service, reasonable profit and the generally prevailing tariff.<br/><br/>Air fare so established by the airlines is published on their respective website under the provision of Sub Rule (2) of Rule 135, Aircraft Rules 1937.<br/><br/>The domestic airline pricing runs in multiple levels (bucket or RBD-Reservation Booking Designator) which are in line with the practice followed globally. Usually, the lower levels of the fare in the fare bucket are assigned to advance purchase (popularly known as Appex Fares) bookings (e.g. up to 90,60,30,14 and 07 days before departure). As time lapses and date of journey approaches closer (from 07 days to date of departure), the fare in higher side of fare bucket are available for purchase.<br/><br/>Airline remains complaint to the regulatory provisions of Rule- 135 as long as the fare charged by them does not exceed the fare established and displayed on their website.<br/><br/>In order to prevent excessive charging and sudden surges in airfares and to promote transparency by scheduled domestic airlines, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has issued Air Transport Circular 02 of 2010 wherein airlines are required to display on their respective websites the tariff sheet route-wise across their network in various fare categories and the manner it is offered in the market.<br/><br/>DGCA has already set up a Tariff Monitoring Unit in 2010 that monitors airfares on certain routes on monthly basis to insure that the airlines do not charge airfares outside the range declared by them. The past analysis has shown that the airfares remained well within the fare bucket uploaded by the airlines on the respective websites.

records.qtitle: Expenditure for improvement of AYUSH infrastructure
records.name: Harivansh

records.ans_text: (a):	 At present 89 posts of Ayurvedic doctors has been sanctioned in the Ministry of AYUSH, to be posted in the Ministry itself and Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS) Dispensaries of Government of India.  Out of 89 posts sanctioned 67 posts are filled. However, the data on the number of AYUSH doctors posted in the hospitals under State/UT Governments is not maintained by Government of India. Further, as per the data received from States/UTs, 7,36,538 registered AYUSH practitioners are available in the country as on 01.04.2014.<br/>(b):    The total plan actual expenditure during   2014-15 is Rs.462.27 Crore for development of AYUSH including AYUSH infrastructure.  <br/>(c):    There is no plan to establish 18 AYUSH Colleges by the Government of India by itself. However, under section 13 A of Indian Medicine Central Council Act, 1970, permission was granted to establish 19 Ayurveda (01 Government and 18 Private) and 02 Unani Private Colleges in the academic session 2014-15.<br/>………..<br/>

records.qtitle: Model schools in backward areas
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	whether the Ministry had formulated a plan to open model schools to provide qualitative education to poor in the backward areas; <br/>(b)	the number of such model schools opened as of now, State-wise; and <br/>(c)	whether the Ministry is formulating any plan to stop the drop-out rate which is maximum among poor; and if so, the details thereof?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT <br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/>(a) :	The Centrally Sponsored Model School Scheme envisages inter alia setting up of 3,500 schools in educationally backward blocks (EBBs) through State/UT Governments. The EBBs have been selected based on twin criteria of Female Rural Literacy rate being below the national average and Gender Gap in literacy being above the national average. However, the Scheme has been delinked from the support of the Government of India with effect from 2015-16 and as such the scheme stands transferred to the States/UTs.<br/> <br/>(b):	Since the launch of the scheme in 2009-10 till 31.3.2015, the Ministry has approved 2490 model schools, out of which 1101 model schools have been made functional. The State-wise details are at Annexure.<br/><br/>(c): 	The Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan (RMSA) scheme implemented by this Ministry which was launched in year 2009 provides for additional classrooms, science laboratory, library, computer room, art/craft/culture room, toilets, drinking water facilities etc in new secondary schools and existing secondary schools, to reduce dropout rate at secondary stage. Interventions like survey and identification of out of school children, awareness programme, bridge courses, special teaching for learning enhancement, residential camp for drop out students have also been supported under RMSA.<br/><br/>	Similarly, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA) programme seeks to provide access, equity, retention and quality in the area of elementary education. Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBY) scheme, which is a part of SSA has the objective to create residential school facilities at the upper primary level for girls belonging predominantly to the SC, ST, OBC and minorities in difficult areas.<br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Criteria for nominated members of CABE
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	the criteria adopted for engagement of nominated members in the Central Advisory Board of Education (CABE);<br/>(b)	the reasons behind the engagement for maximum people of similar thought; and<br/>(c)	whether Government is going forward to bring changes in the education policy of the country and if so, the level at which the suggestions have been sought from the educationists for changes?  <br/><br/>
records.ans_text: <br/>MINISTER OF HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT<br/><br/>(SMT. SMRITI ZUBIN IRANI)<br/><br/><br/>(a)	& (b): Central Advisory Board of Education (CABE) has been reconstituted vide Resolution dated 11.06.2015 for a period of three years from the date of notification. Members representing different interests viz a viz industry, special interest (SC/ST/PWD), minority institutions and eminent educationists, technologists, scientists, experts in school education/ creative arts/ languages etc. are nominated on CABE in order to facilitate decisions keeping in view the interests of all groups.<br/>	<br/>(c): The Government has initiated the process of formulating a New Education Policy to meet the changing dynamics of the population’s requirement with regard to quality education, innovation and research, aiming to make India a knowledge superpower by equipping its students with the necessary skills and knowledge and to eliminate the shortage of manpower in science, technology, academics and industry. Multiple level consultative processes involving all stakeholders, such as, educationists, teachers, and students across all levels are envisaged. The online consultation process has already been launched on www.MyGov.in portal and a huge number of suggestions have already been received on 33 identified themes that are accessible on www.MyGov.in portal. The grass roots level consultation from the Gram Panchayat level through the Block & District to State level is also proposed to be started shortly. Suggestions have also been invited from educationists from all over the country in this regard.<br/><br/>******<br/>

records.qtitle: Investment for long term development
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)  whether the Ministry is planning to invest five hundred billion dollars in Railways in the coming ten to twelve years for the long term development of the country;  <br/><br/>(b)   the quantum of investment made in Railways in the last one year and the quantum of domestic and foreign capital therein; <br/><br/>(c)  whether an investment of five hundred billion dollars is possible in view of its current status; and<br/><br/>(d)  the number of railway projects pending due to shortage of funds and the future plan of the Ministry to complete them?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RAILWAYS<br/><br/>(SHRI MANOJ SINHA)<br/><br/><br/>(a) to (c): No plan to invest US $ 500 billion in the Railways in next ten to twelve years has been prepared. However, an investment of ? 8,56,020 crore (approximately 135 billion US dollars) has been planned for next five years. <br/><br/>The annual plan (Revised Estimate) of the Railways for 2014-15 was ? 65,798 crore. This was financed through Gross Budgetary Support, Internally Generated Resources and Extra Budgetary Resources like market borrowings etc.<br/><br/>(d): Railways has over three hundred ongoing new line, gauge conversion and doubling projects with a throw forward of ? 3.5 lakh crore.<br/> <br/>*****<br/>

records.qtitle: Development of agriculture marketing infrastructure
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)	 whether Government has any plan for development of agriculture marketing infrastructure, if so, the details thereof;<br/><br/>(b)	 whether Government is considering to repeal APMC Act in order to improve agricultural market;<br/><br/>(c) 	whether farmers'' access to agricultural market will increase with the co-operation of private sector, if so, whether any study has been carried out in this regard; and<br/><br/>(d) 	whether there is any plan to make an integrated market at national level, if so, the details thereof?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE <br/><br/>(SHRI MOHANBHAI  KUNDARIA)<br/><br/>(a):	 In order to promote development of agriculture marketing infrastructure, Government has been providing financial assistance through various central sector and centrally sponsored schemes of Department of Agriculture & Cooperation (DAC) such as the Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing (lSAM) and its sub-schemes of Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) and Venture Capital Assistance (VCA) , the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) and the Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) and the scheme of Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI) on Cold Chain, Value Addition and Preservation Infrastructure. Further, the Government has also been advocating to the States/Union Territories to reform their agri¬-marketing laws to promote development of alternative marketing channels other than the Agriculture Produce Market Committee (APMC) market yards to inter-alia promote private investment in development of agri marketing infrastructure. <br/><br/>(b):	 No, Sir.<br/><br/>(c):	 Setting up of private markets in addition to regulated markets will enhance farmers'' access to agriculture markets. As per National Commission on Farmers'' Report (2006) a regulated market should be available to farmers within a radius of 5 Km (corresponding market area of about 80 sq. Km.) while presently average area served by a regulated market in India is 462.19 sq Km. <br/><br/>(d):	 In order to create an integrated market at national level, Government has formulated a Central Sector Scheme for "Promotion of National Agriculture Market through Agri-Tech Infrastructure Fund (ATIF)" to be implemented with a budgetary outlay of Rs.200.00 crores during 2015-16 to 2017-18. Under the scheme, an appropriate common e-market platform would be deployed in 585 selected regulated wholesale markets in states across the country. Department of Agriculture and Cooperation (DAC) will meet expenses on software and its customisation for the States and in addition will also give grant as one time fixed cost subject to the ceiling of Rs.30.00 lakhs per Mandi for related hardware including equipment/infrastructure. <br/>**********<br/>

records.qtitle: Welfare of tribal women
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that there is a decline in the Child Sex Ratio (CSR) in the tribal areas; <br/>(b)	the details of the efforts being made by Government to prevent the declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR) in the tribal areas;<br/>(c) 	the details of the funds allocated under the schemes being run for the welfare of the tribal women, State-wise; and<br/>(d)	the details of the steps being taken by Government to prevent malnutrition in the tribal women?<br/>
records.ans_text: MINISTER OF WOMEN AND CHILD DEVELOPMENT<br/>(SHRIMATI MANEKA SANJAY GANDHI)<br/><br/><br/>(a):    	As per the Census 2011, the Child Sex Ratio (0-6 years) among Scheduled tribes population has shown a decline from 972 females per 1000 males in 2001 to 957 females per 1000 males in 2011.  <br/><br/>(b) 	& (c):  To address the issue of declining Child Sex Ratio (CSR), in age group of 0-6 years, Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP) programme has been launched by Ministry of Women and Child Development. The Scheme is intended to improve Child Sex Ratio across the country with the focussed intervention & Multi-Sectoral Action in 100 gender critical districts including tribal areas. The total project cost of the programme for the 2 years and 6 months is Rs. 199.99 crore with 100% Central Assistance. <br/><br/>The Ministry of Tribal Affairs in consonance of Article 275 (1) of the constitution of India the Government ensures welfare of women while providing grants to the States/ Union Territories under Special Central Assistance to the Tribal Sub-Plan. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs implements schemes, which are focused on the upliftment of tribal girls and women in the field of education and employment. Details of the funds allocated under the schemes being run for the welfare of the tribal population including tribal women are as under:- <br/><br/>S.No 	Programmes/Schemes	Budget Allocation (BE) 2015-16 (In Crore)<br/>1	Strengthening Education among Scheduled Tribe Girls in Low Literacy Districts	40.00<br/>2	National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) including Adivasi Mahila Sashaktikaran Yojana (AMSY)	70.00<br/>3	SCA to TSP	1250.00<br/>4	Grants under Article 275 (1) 	1367.00<br/>5	Umbrella Scheme for Education 	1136.84<br/>6	National Overseas Scholarship	1.00<br/><br/>(d): 	Ministry of Tribal Affairs through regional consultations and its meetings has advocated and supported growing and consumption of traditional minor millets, green leafy and traditional vegetable in kitchen garden, rearing backyard poultry, and fishery. In addition, the Ministry has advocated regular administering of Iron Folic Acid tablets and Vitamin A supplements to pregnant women right from their cycle. Documentation of tribal crops and food, tribal medicine and practices to improve health and nutrition issues has also been initiated. <br/><br/><br/>****<br/>

records.qtitle: Nuclear scientists died mysteriously
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a)the number of nuclear scientists who died under mysterious circumstances during last five years;<br/><br/>(b)the details of the safety measures provided to the scientists to protect them from nuclear radiation; and<br/><br/>(c)the details of Government’s plan to tackle with any untoward situations caused in the nuclear plants?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES & PENSIONS AND PRIME MINISTER’S OFFICE (Dr. JITENDRA SINGH):<br/><br/>(a)The number of nuclear scientists who died in unnatural circumstances mainly relating to road accidents and suicides for the period from 01.01.2010 to 15.07.2015 are 12.<br/><br/>(b)Safety of occupational workers in nuclear facilities is considered as one of the top priorities during the design, construction and operation of nuclear facilities. The plants are designed with engineered safety features and administrative controls to ensure that the persons working in the plant are radiologically protected. Safety standards, stipulated by Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), are meticulously followed as per national and international standards. Regular monitoring of ambient radiation levels, air activity and contamination levels are carried out under the supervision of Radiological Safety Officer (RSO) appointed by AERB. Necessary protective equipments are provided to plant personnel to ensure radiological safety. Personnel dosimetry programme is in place to ensure that radiological exposure are much below the prescribed limits. <br/><br/>(c)Nuclear Facilities in India are designed, constructed, commissioned and operated in conformity with relevant nuclear safety requirements. These requirements ensure an adequate margin of safety so that nuclear facilities can be operated without undue radiological risks to the plant personnel and members of the public. Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) plans are developed as a measure of abundant caution in accordance with the national and international laws and regulations and to deal with effective management of any eventuality. The efficacy of EPR is tested by conducting emergency exercises regularly. Government of India has enacted Disaster Management Act for prevention and mitigation of all disasters including Nuclear and Radiological Emergencies. 												                                    *****<br/>

records.qtitle: Constitution of NICDA
records.name: Harivansh
records.qn_text: (a) 	whether it is a fact that the Ministry is planning to take the approval of the Cabinet for the constitution of National Industrial Corridor Development Authority (NICDA) for the development of industrial corridors;<br/><br/>(b) 	whether the objective of Government behind this step is to accelerate the manufacturing and to develop India as a global hub;<br/><br/>(c) 	the total land required for the development of industrial corridors;<br/><br/>(d) 	the estimated cost on the development of such corridors; and<br/><br/>(e) 	the benefits expected to the manufacturing sector and the employment opportunities to be generated from these industrial corridors?<br/><br/>
records.ans_text: THE MINISTER OF STATE (INDEPENDENT CHARGE)<br/>OF THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY<br/>(SHRIMATI NIRMALA SITHARAMAN)<br/><br/>(a):     Yes, Sir.<br/><br/><br/>(b):	The Government of India has adopted the strategy of developing integrated Industrial Corridors in partnership with State Governments to accelerate manufacturing. The formation of the National Industrial Corridor Development Authority will enable the development and implementation of Industrial Corridor Projects across India.  <br/><br/>(c):	As per current stage of planning, Land required for development of identified nodes in the industrial corridors is given as under:<br/><pre><br/><br/>	Name of the Node	State	Area<br/>(in Sq.km.)<br/>Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC)*	Dadri-Noida-Ghaziabad Investment Region	Uttar Pradesh	210<br/>	Manesar-Bawal Investment Region	Haryana	402<br/>	Khushkhera-Bhiwadi-Neemrana Investment Region	Rajasthan	160<br/>	Pithampur-Dhar-Mhow Investment Region	Madhya Pradesh	372<br/>	Ahmedabad-Dholera Investment Region	Gujarat	920<br/>	Shendra Bidkin Investment Region	Maharashtra	84<br/>	Dighi Port Industrial Area	Maharashtra	253<br/>	Jodhpur Pali Marwar Industrial Area	Rajasthan	155<br/>Chennai Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC)	Tumkur	Karnataka	38.96		<br/>	Ponneri	Tamil Nadu	88.93		<br/>	Krishnapatnam	Andhra Pradesh	48.01		<br/>Note   * relates to Phase-I of DMIC project 		<br/></pre><br/><br/> (d):	The development of Industrial Corridors is to be undertaken in phased manner.  The Government of India approved the financial and institutional structure and financial assistance for the development of industrial cities in DMIC in September 2011. The financial assistance will be in the form of grant of Rs. 17,500 crore over five years for the development of industrial cities @ Rs. 2500 crore per city on an average subject to a ceiling of Rs. 3000 crore per city. The Japanese Government has also announced financial support to an extent of US $ 4.5 billion in the first phase of the DMIC project.<br/><br/>(e):	The Industrial Corridors aim at attracting domestic and foreign direct investment in manufacturing and infrastructure, putting in place a holistic planning and development approach, while taking advantage of the inherent strengths and competitiveness of the States included in the Industrial Corridors; Providing “best in class” infrastructure including internal and external trunk infrastructure, effective and efficient transportation, reliable energy supplies, ICT (Information Communication and Technology) and efficient logistics; Development of smart Industrial Cities of the future which can be benchmarked as the best in the world; Upgrading & developing the skills of the workforce and creating employment opportunities; and Promoting sustainable development and inclusive growth.  <br/><br/>****<br/>
